1.name: Ja'Marr Chase
1.comment: Chase saw his numbers dip a little last year, mainly because the Bengals had some quarterback issues because of injury. But even with the inconsistent quarterback play, Chase was fourth overall run fantasy receiver scoring and led the league in targets (185). Chase had at least 100 receptions for the third straight season. He had eight games with 20-plus fantasy points. Another positive was Chase dropped a career-low four passes despite leading the league in targets. A healthy Joe Burrow should are a huge plus for Chase this coming year. These two have a great connection. Chase has five straight 1,000-yard seasons and might be the best receiver in the game right now. He is in the prime of his career. Chase has great hands and is a good route runner. He lacks elite speed but that has not held him back. He plays faster than his timed speed. Chase is the complete package at receiver.
1.outlook: Cincinnati Bengals Ja'Marr Chase was one of the top players in fantasy football last season, catching 125 of 185 targets for 1,412 yards, eight touchdowns, and adding 14 rushing yards on three attempts across 16 games. He owned 30.5% of the team's targets and 34.8% of the team's air yards, but his average depth of target was only 8.3%. The Bengals offense will be explosive again, and with a defense expected to be at the bottom of the league, it's a recipe for fantasy gold. Key pieces such as wide receiver Tee Higgins and running back Chase Brown are returning in 2026. Chase's fantasy value relies on the health of star quarterback Joe Burrow, who was limited to eight appearances last year due to a toe injury. However, he did have great chemistry with Joe Flacco when he was filling in for Burrow, racking up a whopping 72 targets in over five games. Flacco is also returning to the Bengals and signed a one-year deal this offseason. With Burrow healthy and Flacco coming back, Chase is set to have another monster season in 2026 and is a top-three pick in fantasy as his Sleeper ADP is currently third overall heading into fantasy football draft season.

2.name: Puka Nacua
2.comment: Nacua had a monster season, leading all fantasy receivers in scoring. He led the league in receptions (129) and set careers highs in all three major categories (receptions, yards and touchdowns). Nacua even missed a game because of injury. He had double-digit fantasy points all but a game and 10 games with 20-plus fantasy points. Nacua had one of the best all-time fantasy receiver seasons, which is saying something. He will continue to be the focal point of the Rams passing attack. He has 100-plus receptions two of three seasons. Nacua really improved catching the ball from earlier in his career, dropping just five passes the last two seasons despite getting a ton of weekly looks. He catches nearly everything thrown his way these days. Nacua is the complete package at receiver. Nacua is a very good athlete. He lacks a little speed, but that doesn't hold him back at all. He makes plenty of big plays. His route running is top notch and his ability to make the tough catch in traffic is second to none.
2.outlook: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua set career highs across the board last season with catches (129), targets (166), receiving yards (1,715), and total touchdowns (11). The only knock on Nacua from last season was that teammate Davante Adams received more looks in the red zone and was targeted 34.8% of the time compared to Nacua's 17.0%. The Rams' core offense is returning in 2026 with Adams, Kyren Williams, Blake Corum, and the team even extended NFL MVP Matthew Stafford to a one-year, $55 million extension this offseason. However, Nacua has had a tumultuous offseason. The 24-year-old is in a civil lawsuit after being accused of biting a woman and making antisemitic remarks, stemming from an incident on December 31. The former fifth-round pick later checked into a rehab facility. Per the star wide receiver's attorney, Levi McCathern, he has been in rehab for a "substantial period" before previous allegations of assault, and "he's scheduled to be there for a while longer." Nacua did report to the Rams' voluntary workouts and is seeking an extension as he enters the final year of his rookie contract. As long as Nacua can stay out of trouble and avoid a suspension, he is a surefire top-five pick in fantasy football and is currently being selected fourth overall on Sleeper.

3.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
3.comment: Smith-Njigba had a breakout season, serving as the clear top target in the Seahawks passing game. He took his game to a new level, finishing second overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He lead the league in receiving yards (1,793) and had 119 receptions. He was as good as any fantasy receiver in the game, having double-digit fantasy points all but a game. He reached 20-plus fantasy points 11 games. Smith-Njigba had one of the best fantasy seasons in recent memory. He has reached 100-plus receptions two straight seasons. Smith-Njigba will continue to be the clear top target for the Seahawks for years to come. Smith-Njigba has great hands and does a good job of making the contested catch. He also makes plays after the catch. His route running still needs a little work but is much improved. And Smith-Njigba rarely drops a pass, having 10 his last two seasons. He has emerged as one of the best receivers in all of football.
3.outlook: Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba signed a four-year, $168.6 million contract extension with the Seahawks during the offseason, making him the highest-paid wide receiver in the NFL. The 24-year-old won Offensive Player of the Year, won a Super Bowl ring, and had great chemistry with quarterback Sam Darnold. JSN caught 119 of 162 targets for 1,793 yards and 10 touchdowns, while rushing for 36 yards on seven attempts in 17 games in 2025. The 24-year-old owned 35.7% of the team's targets, 106.2 air yards per game, and averaged 4.6 yards after the catch. What's even more amazing about JSN's season is that the Seahawks ranked 29th in passing attempts last year. Seattle's offense could take a step back as Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III signed with the Chiefs during free agency, and offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak is now the head coach of the Las Vegas Raiders. The Seahawks have most of their offense returning with Cooper Kupp, Rashid Shaheed, Zach Charbonnet (knee), and the team selected running back Jadarian Price in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft. JSN will look to make it back-to-back seasons as one of the top wideouts in fantasy and is currently going fifth overall on Sleeper, which aligns perfectly with his fifth overall ranking at RotoBaller.

4.name: Justin Jefferson
4.comment: Jefferson had a season to forget last year, finishing with a career low in yards (1,048). The Vikings had all sorts of issues at quarterback, leading to his inconsistent numbers. Jefferson had always got it done despite quarterback issues throughout his career but couldn't overcome them last year. Jefferson finished just 20th overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He only had one game all year with 20-plus points. The Vikings addressed the quarterback problem this offseason, bringing in Kyler Murray. This should be an upgrade for the team. Jefferson has six straight 1,000-yard seasons to start his career and had 100-plus receptions three of those seasons. He is just 27 years old and in the prime of his career. Jefferson is the clear top target in an offense that knows how to get him the ball. Jefferson is the complete package at receiver. He has great hands and is a top route runner that just has a knack for getting open. He catches nearly every thrown his way and rarely drops a pass despite getting a ton of work.
4.outlook: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson and quarterback JJ McCarthy couldn't get on the same page last season, limiting Jefferson to the worst season of his career. The 26-year-old caught 84 of 144 targets for two touchdowns while adding seven yards on two rushes. He owned 30.2% of the team's target shares, but it took 144 targets for Jefferson to log his fifth-straight 1,000-yard campaign. Before last year, Jefferson averaged 99 catches for 1,486 yards and eight touchdowns in his previous five seasons. He was plagued by poor quarterback play, which also limited other top offensive weapons, wide receiver Jordan Addison and tight end T.J. Hockenson. Before 2025, Minnesota had high-octane offenses under head coach Kevin O'Connell, and the team is set to turn things around this season with most of the offense returning. The Vikings signed Kyler Murray to a one-year deal in March after the Cardinals released him. Murray will compete with McCarthy for the Vikings' starting quarterback job. The former No. 1 overall pick will look to revitalize his career and get Jefferson back on track as an elite fantasy WR1. Jefferson's fantasy value solely relies on whether McCarthy or Murray can bounce back. At RotoBaller, he's currently ranked as WR6 and is projected to rack up 108 catches for 1,395 yards and eight touchdowns in 2026, making him a borderline first-round pick heading into 2026 fantasy football drafts.

5.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
5.comment: St. Brown finished third overall in fantasy receiver scoring for the third straight season. He continues to post huge numbers as the No. 1 target in the Lions high-powered offense. St. Brown had 117 receptions for 1,401 yards and 11 touchdowns. He has three straight seasons with 115-plus receptions, 1,200-plus yards and double-digit touchdowns. There are not many more consistent fantasy receivers in football right now than St. Brown. He had double-digit fantasy points all but four games and topped 20 points seven times. St. Brown is one of the best receivers in the NFL. And he seems to be getting better with more seasoning, which is scary for the rest of the league. St. Brown is not an explosive player but runs top-notch routes and has great hands. He is not going to wow you in any one area but makes plays and gets open. He just gets it done. St. Brown catches nearly everything thrown his way, having just 27 drops in four seasons on 742 targets.
5.outlook: Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown has finished as the WR3 for three consecutive seasons in Half-PPR formats, and he remains one of the safest selections in the first round of 2026 fantasy drafts. He is the only player to reach 115 receptions in each of the past three seasons, and his 33 red zone targets in 2025 led the league, while only Davante Adams saw more looks from within the 10. The Lions added very little in the way of pass-catchers through either free agency or the NFL Draft, and even with tight end Sam LaPorta expected back and healthy after undergoing surgery to repair a herniated disc, St. Brown's status as a true target-dominator remains unchallenged. Playing in his fifth professional season, St. Brown saw a career-high 31.2% target share in 2025, and that number could again be on the rise under new offensive coordinator Drew Petzing. Only two current playcallers used more multi-tight end sets than Petzing in 2025, and if that trend continues in Detroit, St. Brown could see an even higher concentration of targets as one of only two wide receivers routinely on the field. Since the start of the 2022 season, Jared Goff has racked up an NFL-leading 18,206 passing yards, with Patrick Mahomes the only other quarterback to top 16,000 yards in that span. Operating as the primary option in what has been, and should continue to be, one of the league's elite offenses, the 26-year-old St. Brown should have no trouble returning first-round value as RotoBaller's WR5.

6.name: Drake London
6.comment: London had injury issues for the first time in his career, missing five games. He produced very well when on the field, though, finishing just 81 yards shy of a 1,000-yard season. If he plays a full year, London has 96 receptions for 1,302 and 10 touchdowns. London had five 100-yard games and two games with 30-plus fantasy points. London has at least 110 targets three straight seasons as the top target in the Falcons offense. The Falcons still have some question marks at quarterback but that hasn't held London back much to date. He is going to rack up the targets in this offense. London has great size for the position and catches nearly everything thrown his way. He can play on the outside or out of the slot. He lacks a little elite speed, but that doesn't seem to hold him back at all.
6.outlook: Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London caught 68 passes for 919 yards and seven touchdowns across 12 games last season. He missed five games with a knee injury, but had elite usage, as he had 21.5% of the team's targets, averaged 2.52 yards per route run, and averaged around 16 fantasy points per week. The 24-year-old signed a four-year $141 million extension with the Falcons this offseason. London will be under a new head coach in Kevin Stefanski, OC Tommy Reese, and a new starting quarterback in Tua Tagovailoa while Michael Penix Jr. (knee) continues to recover from an ACL tear. Despite being in a new offensive system, the Falcons offense will revolve around running back Bijan Robinson, Kyle Pitts, and London again in 2026. It will be the third time in his five-year career that London will be under a new offense, but fantasy managers can expect another solid season from London due to his high usage. RotoBaller is on board with London having a top-10 season, and projects 93 catches for 1,193 yards and seven touchdowns, making him a mid-second-round pick in upcoming fantasy football drafts.

7.name: Chris Olave
7.comment: The Saints solved their quarterback dilemma, which led to a big season from Olave. He was sixth overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He set career highs in receptions (100), yards (1,163) and touchdowns (nine). He had double-digit fantasy points all but two games. Olave was a consistent factor all season long in the Saints offense. He should continue to be the top target for quarterback Tyler Shough going forward. Olave has 1,000-yard seasons three of four. He has concussion concerns and could be one big hit away from never playing again but last year was a big step forward for him. Olave is a great downfield threat. He can get to the next level in a hurry. He also isn't just a deep threat. He runs solid routes and can make plays after the catch. Olave lacks a little strength and will drop the occasional pass (20 in four seasons).
7.outlook: New Orleans Saints wide receiver Chris Olave is coming off the best season of his career and entering 2026 as a low-end WR1 for fantasy. During the 2025 season, Olave emerged as the true WR1 in this offense, drawing an impressive 156 targets (the fifth-most in football) and catching 100 of them for 1,163 yards and nine touchdowns. Given that New Orleans lacked many proven pass catchers opposite Olave for most of the season (after trading Rashid Shaheed), Olave was given a large share of the passing attack. His production was also very impressive, as Olave appeared in just eight games the previous season due to several concussions. Seeing him quickly regain his WR1 floor and posting the best season of his career was an excellent sign. However, Olave's volume will likely decline in 2026, which makes him a somewhat risky selection at his ADP. In the opening round of the 2026 NFL Draft, the Saints addressed their No. 2 WR position by selecting Jordyn Tyson out of Arizona State. Tyson has dealt with injuries in college as well, but is more than capable of emerging as an every-down option at the professional level. While the Saints offense under Kellen Moore will often opt to push the ball downfield in 2026 (sixth-most pass attempts last season), the signing of Travis Etienne Jr. will give them a stable rushing attack, and the addition of Tyson will draw targets away from Olave. Given the upgrades to the offense roster, Olave should be viewed as a high-end WR2, but is going off the board as the WR11 (24th overall) in current PPR drafts on Sleeper.

8.name: CeeDee Lamb
8.comment: Lamb didn't have quite the season most hoped, missing three games because of injury while scoring just three touchdowns. He did average a career-best 14.4 yards per reception. And he was 21st overall in fantasy receiver scoring. Lamb had six 100-yard games and double-digit fantasy points all but three games. He did have George Pickens to compete with for targets, which likely led to his somewhat down production. Lamb has five straight 1,000-yard seasons. Lamb is in the prime of his career and the top target in an offense that likes to throw the ball. Lamb is a complete receiver at this stage of his career. He has good size, runs solid routes and has plus hands. He is a big-play threat at the position. Lamb does have some drop issues, dropping eight passes last year.
8.outlook: Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb appeared in 14 games last season but was hampered by injuries throughout parts of the year, resulting in the least productive fantasy campaign of his career. Even so, Lamb eclipsed 1,000 receiving yards for the fifth consecutive season and led Dallas in targets per game. The team's overall leader in total targets, however, was George Pickens, who erupted for more than 1,400 yards and nine touchdowns in his first season with the Cowboys. Entering 2026, there will undoubtedly be debate over which Dallas receiver should come off the board first in fantasy drafts, but Lamb is still likely to be the preferred option in most formats given his longer track record of success with quarterback Dak Prescott. The last time Lamb and Prescott both played all 17 games, Lamb finished as the fantasy WR1 while recording one of the most prolific receiving seasons in NFL history in 2023. Prescott has supported multiple top-24 fantasy receivers on several occasions throughout his career, and fantasy managers should feel confident that head coach Brian Schottenheimer will continue to lean on a high-powered passing attack. With his rare combination of high floor and elite ceiling, Lamb should remain a strong target within the first 15 picks of most fantasy drafts.

9.name: George Pickens
9.comment: A move to Dallas was a great one for Pickens, who had a career season. He was fourth overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He had 93 receptions for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns. Pickens had double-digit fantasy points all but three games, topping 20 points five times. It was quite the season for Pickens. He also dropped just four passes despite on 137 targets. Pickens had better numbers than fellow teammate CeeDee Lamb. These guys will continue to be the one-two punch for the Cowboys passing game. Pickens has 1,000-yard seasons two of three. He is one of the top deep threats in football. Pickens has really good hands and a knack for the acrobatic catch. He gets in and out of his breaks in a hurry. He has a tendency of being inconsistent and immature, but that wasn't an issues in Dallas last year.
9.outlook: Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens put together his long-awaited breakout campaign in 2025. After showing flashes of immense upside with the Steelers over the first three seasons of his career, he took a massive step forward when joining forces with Dak Prescott and the Cowboys. During his first campaign in the NFC East, the former George Bulldog caught 93 passes for 1,429 yards and nine scores. Overall, Pickens was the WR6 in PPR scoring and finished third at his position in total receiving yards, making him one of the best values on the board in 2025 fantasy drafts. In the offseason, there was some growing speculation that the Cowboys could consider moving on from Pickens, but both sides agreed to the franchise tag, which keeps him under contract for the 2026 campaign. As a result, the 25-year-old enters the 2026 campaign as a borderline WR1 given that his situation has remained fairly constant. Even though he will be sharing the field with another superstar wideout in CeeDee Lamb, Prescott is able to support both of them, given the nature of the games the Cowboys play. In 2025, the Cowboys surrendered 30.1 PPG (the most in football), which forced them to drive the ball downfield. While they did take strides in improving this unit, managers should not expect a drastic shift in just one season. Given his role in the Dallas offense that threw the ball the third-most times in football last season, fantasy managers should feel comfortable selecting Pickens at his current Sleeper ADP of 23, going off the board as the No. 10 WR.

10.name: Nico Collins
10.comment: Collins had his third straight 1,000-yard season as the top target for the Texans passing attack. He was eighth overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He had some huge games, topping 20 fantasy points five times. He was a little up and down in a passing attack that was shaky at times. Collins had fewer than double-digit fantasy points five times. Collins will continue to be the top target for the Texans and get plenty of work in that role. Collins is a big receiver with good size and speed. He is a good route runner that gets off the line well because of his strength. He can be a tough cover. Injuries are a concern after missing plenty of action each of his first fivevseasons in the NFL.
10.outlook: Houston Texans wide receiver Nico Collins has seen his fantasy upside limited due to injuries, but when on the field, he has produced at a WR1 level. Following two quiet seasons to begin his career, Collins turned in a Year 3 breakout in 2023 and has remained Houston's WR1 ever since. During the 2025 season, Collins appeared in 15 games and brought in 71 of his 120 targets for 1,117 yards and six touchdowns. His target total placed him 15th among all WRs, despite the missed time, and also marked the highest total of his career. The 27-year-old makes the most of his receptions, flashing high upside in the downfield game as he caught 18 passes for more than 20 yards and added another five for more than 40 yards, marking the second time in the past three years he has hit these marks. The lone knock on his fantasy profile has always been his injury history, as he has never played in more than 15 games in a single season and even fell short of that mark in 2024. Entering 2026, Collins once again projects to see a high target share as the clear WR1 in this offense. Even though second-year pass catchers Jayden Higgins and Jaylin Noel may eventually carve out a role, Collins' connection with C.J. Stroud should give him a major edge. While playing on a team that will look to lean on its rushing attack (13th-most rushing attempts in 2025), his high target share provides him a safe floor, and his YAC ability boosts his ceiling. Collins' current Sleeper ADP of 21 (WR9) is a fine price for those opting to fade the elite tier of the position.

11.name: A.J. Brown
11.comment: Brown hit the 1,000-yard mark for the fourth straight season despite missing a couple games and totally disappearing in a few others. He had enough big games to finish with solid numbers once again. Brown was 12th overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He had five 100-yard games and double-digit fantasy points 10 of 15 games. Brown was upset with his usage throughout the season but still managed to have another very good fantasy season. He has been a top-10 fantasy receiver four of seven seasons. Brown heads to the suddenly explosive Patriots offense to take over their No. 1 receiving duties. Brown is good at getting in an out of his breaks. He can make a big play in a hurry, averaging 15.3 yards per reception for his career. He runs solid routes and can do well on the outside and the slot. Brown is a big, strong receiver with top speed, making him one of the toughest covers in all of football. He also has great hands, dropping just one pass the last two years.
11.outlook: Newly acquired New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown was the focal point of one of the largest trades of the offseason. After being linked to the Patriots for several months, the Eagles finally opted to send their WR1 to New England to join MVP runner-up Drake Maye. Even though Brown expressed frustration with the Eagles' offense throughout the 2025 season, the wideout still turned in a productive campaign, catching 78 of his 121 targets for 1,003 yards and seven touchdowns. This stat line made him the overall WR11 in PPR scoring and marked the second time over his past three seasons in which Brown finished as a top-12 option at the position. Brown has been a stable force in the red zone, scoring seven touchdowns in three straight seasons and drawing at least 120 targets in two of his last three, despite playing in a run-heavy offense. Brown should see his fantasy ceiling rise significantly, joining Maye, who finished as the QB2 as a sophomore despite lacking a true WR1 in his offense. Brown will now slide in as the top option for Maye, sharing the field with Romeo Doubs and Kayshon Boutte. Even though the Patriots leaned on their rushing attack in 2025 (sixth-most rushing attempts in the sport), bringing in a true WR1 to this offense will help them drive the ball downfield. Playing with one of the game's premier passers should keep Brown firmly in the WR1 tier, making him a great selection going off the board as the WR12 (28.0 ADP) on PPR Sleeper drafts for those who opt to target the running back position early in their drafts.

12.name: Malik Nabers
12.comment: Nabers tore his ACL in Week 4, missing much of last year. He made his mark before getting hurt, though, having 18 receptions for 271 yards and two touchdowns before the unfortunate injury. Nabers has a long road back but was hurt early enough last year that there is a good chance he is ready for the start of this season. He will be the top target for second-year quarterback Jaxon Dart, who his a huge plus for Nabers going forward. Nabers topped 100 receptions and 1,200 yards his rookie season, showing his huge talent. Nabers is a receiver that can get it done at all three levels. He has top speed and athleticism. Nabers also does well with the contested catch and is a great leaper. He will drop some passes, having nine drops his rookie season. He is the pretty complete package at receiver, though, and should just keep getting better with more seasoning.
12.outlook: New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers (knee) suffered ACL and meniscus tears in Week 4's game against the Los Angeles Chargers, prematurely ending his season. Nabers caught 18 passes for 271 yards and two touchdowns over four games before the season-ending injury. The 22-year-old initially had the knee surgery in late October and had a procedure in April to remove scar tissue. He continues to progress and is expected to return to the field soon. According to head coach John Harbaugh, he's making "really good progress," and he's "very hopeful that he'll be back soon." Harbaugh added that Nabers is 70-80 percent through his rehab process. Barring a setback, Nabers will likely be ready by the time training camp rolls around. Some of the offseason changes besides the addition of HC Harbaugh include new OC Charles Nagy, wide receiver Darnell Mooney, and tight end Isaiah Likely. All of Nabers' production, except Week 4, came with now-retired quarterback Russell Wilson. The Giants' offense was gradually better with then-rookie QB Jaxson Dart. Nabers is targeting a Week 1 return and should produce with Dart as long as he's healthy. RotoBaller ranks the former first-round pick as WR18 and projects 77 catches, 1,103 yards, and seven touchdowns in 2026. Fantasy managers should continue to monitor Nabers' progress throughout training camp, but all signs are pointing up for the LSU product heading into fantasy football drafts.

13.name: D.J. Moore
13.comment: Moore had the worst season of his career in the Bears new offense. He struggled to carve out a consistent role and get on the same page as Caleb Williams. Moore was just 34th overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He had 50 receptions for 682 yards and six touchdowns. Moore did have six games with double-digit fantasy points, topping 20 points four times. So he had some big showings to go along with his down games. Moore gets a chance for a fresh start this year with the Bills, becoming their go-to target in the passing game. A move to Buffalo could get Moore back to his big ways. Moore has 1,000-yard seasons four of seven. He is a fast receiver with good moves in space. He catches the ball very well and does well on shorter or longer routes. He lacks a little size but makes up for that with his hands and play after the catch. Moore did look disinterested at times last year, which led to his inconsistent play.
13.outlook: There's quite a bit of optimism in upstate New York: Josh Allen is the best quarterback DJ Moore has ever played with. Conversely, Moore is the best receiver that Allen has had to throw to since Stefon Diggs left the Bills. Facing less target competition and with a better offense, fantasy managers hope he can rebound as a WR2, a status that evaded him last season. Moore had one of his best seasons under Buffalo head coach Joe Brady when the pair teamed up in Carolina in 2020, but he's now 29 years old, and advanced metrics may point to a receiver losing a half-step (74th in yards per route run in 2025). The Bills are, as currently constructed, also a run-first football team. Moore may not be dominant enough to command targets as Diggs did, but he will be the preferred option in the Buffalo offensive machine, and that alone warrants a fourth or fifth round pick.

14.name: Luther Burden III
14.comment: Burden did not get a lot of playing time the first half of his rookie year but emerged the second half of the season and was a huge part of the offense down the stretch. He had double-digit fantasy points three of his last four games. And he was targeted 14 times in the Bears two playoff games. Despite playing little early in the year, Burden still managed 47 receptions for 652 yards and two touchdowns, making a lot of big plays. With D.J. Moore gone this season, Burden has a real chance to be the top receiver in this explosive Bears offense. Burden is great after the catch and can get to the next level in a hurry with the ball in his hands. He also is very good at the acrobatic, tough catch. He will drop some passes, though, and isn't always great at the contested catch.
14.outlook: Burden is ready to take a huge step forward this season. He is a fantasy player on the rise and could end up being a low-end No. 1 for fantasy teams if everything falls into place for him this year. A breakout season seems likely for Burden. He can get 90 receptions for 1,200 yards and eight touchdowns.

15.name: Zay Flowers
15.comment: Despite dealing with erratic quarterback play, Flowers had his best season to date. He was seventh overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He had his second straight 1,000-yard season, finishing with 86 receptions for 1,211 yards and six total touchdowns. A lack of scores held him back a little but his fantasy numbers were still very good. Flowers had 74-plus receptions three straight seasons as the top target in the Ravens passing game. He will continue to lead the way for Baltimore's passing attack. Flowers lacks size, but is a playmaker. He is a good route runner that can make plays in the open field. Flowers plays really fast. He does lack a little size and strength, but that has slowed him little to date.
15.outlook: Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers quietly finished the 2025 season as the WR7 in Half-PPR formats, though he got there largely on the back of three massive games. Flowers opened the year with a career-high 143 receiving yards and a touchdown in a primetime matchup with the Bills. He would top 120 yards in two other contests, but the 8.8 fantasy points he averaged across his remaining 14 games would have landed him at WR40. Flowers has seen his targets, receptions, and yards rise each year in the league, but he has never topped five touchdowns in a season, and with much of his production tending to come from scattered boom games, his off weeks can be devastating, finishing with fewer than 5.5 points eight times over the past two seasons. The Ravens have shaken up their coaching staff ahead of the 2026 season, and new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle, who previously served as an assistant under Ben Johnson, arrived in Baltimore with a stated goal of creating more explosive plays. With the Ravens allowing two of their more explosive playmakers, Isaiah Likely and Keaton Mitchell, to walk in free agency, Flowers projects to be a focal point of that scheme. Baltimore spent third and fourth-round picks on USC's Ja'Kobi Lane and Indiana's Elijah Sarratt, and three-time Pro Bowl tight end Mark Andrews signed a three-year extension in December, so Flowers still does not project to see the steady volume needed to support the healthy floor of some of the other receivers going in his range of drafts. At RotoBaller's WR19, he will not always be the model of consistency, but for rosters built to handle his boom-or-bust nature, Flowers can single-handedly deliver several week-winning performances.

16.name: Tetairoa McMillan
16.comment: McMillan had a really solid rookie season, finishing 14th overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He hit the 1,000-yard mark in year one. He was very consistent, scoring double-digit fantasy points 12 of 17 games. McMillan emerged as the clear top target for Bryce Young and should be the No. 1 receiver in this offense for years to come. McMillan is a big receiver that does a great job on contested catches. He runs solid routes and has plus hands. McMillan also is good at making plays after the catch. He is a pretty complete overall receiver for a young player. McMillan did have some drop issues last year, dropping eight passes.
16.outlook: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan was selected with the eighth overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft and was immediately pushed into the WR1 role in the Carolina offense. In his debut campaign, McMillan saw 122 targets and brought in 70 of them for 1,014 yards and seven touchdowns. His lower reception total gave him a slight boost in half-PPR scoring as he finished as the WR15, compared to the WR16 in PPR leagues. In the offseason, the Panthers did not make any major additions to the wide receiver room, leaving the Arizona product as the clear WR1, as he will share the field with unproven options such as Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette. While both have shown upside at times, they have yet to operate as a true complement in this offense over a full 17-game season. While his target share should keep his floor stable, McMillan's ceiling could be much higher in his second season. Down the stretch, his QB, Bryce Young, showed steady progression as he averaged 214 yards per game over his last seven contests, compared to the pedestrian 166 yards per game over the first nine games. Even though McMillan carries a high price tag in relation to his rookie performance (WR15) at an ADP of 33.0 in PPR Sleeper drafts, his massive projected volume and improving quarterback will set him up to contend for a WR1 campaign.

17.name: Garrett Wilson
17.comment: Wilson had a knee injury in Week 6 that cut short his season. He tried to return Week 10 but was unable to finish the game and was held out the rest of the season, playing just seven games. He had 36 receptions for 395 yards and four touchdowns, finishing with 20-plus fantasy points three games. Wilson somehow keeps producing well despite getting terrible quarterback play most years. He could be setup for a similar situation this year. Wilson had three straight 1,000-yard seasons before last year. Wilson is a playmaker. He has top speed and can make a big play in a hurry. Wilson is good at making plays after the catch. He will drop a few passes, though, having 22 in four seasons.
17.outlook: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson was enjoying an impressive start to the 2025 campaign before suffering a knee injury. Over his first five games, Wilson would total more than 19.0 PPR points in all but one before suffering this injury in Week 6. While Wilson would return to action in Week 10, the former first-round pick would then face a setback and not suit up for the remainder of the campaign. During his first six games (removing his Week 10 showing), Wilson continued to operate as the clear WR1 in a weak Jets passing attack, drawing 9.3 targets per game. Throughout most of his time in New York, Wilson has served as the undisputed WR1, which has provided him a high floor in fantasy, even though he has typically had subpar play under center. While the QB situation once again has questions in 2026 with veteran Geno Smith slated to take over after posting a rough 19:17 TD:INT with just 3,025 yards over 15 games with the Raiders last season, Wilson faces far more target competition than he did last fall. In the 2026 NFL Draft, the Jets added two premier pass catchers in the opening round, selecting top tight end Kenyon Sadiq and wideout Omar Cooper Jr. Additionally, the team's current WR2, Adonai Mitchell, a former first-round talent, showed promise down the stretch in 2025, seeing 8.6 targets per game and tallying 52.0 yards per game over his last five contests. While Wilson should remain the top option in this offense, Smith's underwhelming QB play and added target competition could limit his upside in 2026. Currently, the former Ohio State Buckeye is going off the board on Sleeper PPR drafts as the WR16 (37.0 ADP), which makes him a high-floor WR2 with limited upside given that the New York passing offense looks far more balanced than it has in years past.

18.name: Emeka Egbuka
18.comment: Egbuka had a great start to his rookie season but stumbled some after Week 5. He had just two games with double-digit fantasy points after Week 5, topping 50 yards just three times. He had 100-yard games two of his first five to start the season, though, and reached double-digit fantasy points all five of those games. Egbuka was 22nd overall in fantasy reliever scoring. He gets a chance to be a full-time starter from day one this year because of the departure of Mike Evans. Egbuka should be a huge part of the Bucs offense for years to come. Egbuka is a good route runner for a young player. He has solid hands and is a load to bring down after the catch. Egbuka is very good after contact. He did struggled with drops his rookie season, having nine, and consistency was an issue.
18.outlook: Egbuka is a fantasy player on the rise. Look for him to build on last year and take another step forward in an expanded role in a pass-heavy offense. Consider him a No. 2 for fantasy teams. Egbuka can get around 90 receptions for 1,200 yards and eight touchdowns.

19.name: Wan'Dale Robinson
19.comment: Robinson had his second straight great season for the Giants. He hit the 1,000-yard mark for the first time in his career. He also had 92 receptions, giving him 90-plus catches two straight seasons. Robinson was 13th overall in fantasy receiver scoring in an offense that had some issues last season. He had 10 of 16 games with double-digit fantasy points. Robinson has really elevated his game in recent years and turned that into a big contract with the Titans, reuniting with Brian Daboll, who is the offensive coordinator. Robinson should be the No. 1 receiver and rack up the targets from second-year starter Cam Ward. Robinson lacks size but is very quick and can make plays after the catch. He is a tough cover out of the slot because of his shiftiness. Robinson can struggle some with press coverage because of his size. He has great hands, though, having just 14 drops in four seasons on 389 targets.
19.outlook: Although he totaled just 10 touchdowns during his four seasons in New York, wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson established himself as a reliable short-yardage option out of the slot. He turned in a career-best campaign last season after stepping into an expanded role with Malik Nabers (knee) sidelined, and the Tennessee Titans rewarded him this offseason with a four-year, $70 million contract. For a brief period, Robinson seemed entrenched as the Titans' WR1, but Tennessee used the fourth overall pick of the 2026 NFL Draft on Ohio State receiver Carnell Tate. While Tate's arrival could prevent Robinson from replicating his 2025 production, it should certainly aid in the development of second-year quarterback Cam Ward. Last year's first overall pick began finding his rhythm in the back half of the season, throwing for more than 1,300 yards and 10 touchdowns against just one interception across his final seven full contests. If Ward and the Titans take a step forward in 2026, Robinson could be a valuable fantasy asset in PPR formats, especially given his familiarity with new OC Brian Daboll's system. The health of 31-year-old Calvin Ridley (leg) is also worth monitoring, but Robinson remains an intriguing late-round fantasy option.

20.name: Rashee Rice
20.comment: Rice played about half a season because of suspension and injury but produced pretty big when on the field. He played eight games and topped 20 fantasy points four times. He had 53 receptions for 571 yards and five touchdowns. If Rice plays a full year, he has 117 receptions for 1,213 yards and 13 total touchdowns. Rice has struggled with injuries throughout his career in addition to the off the field stuff but he is the clear No. 1 for the Chiefs. Rice is the complete package at receiver. He has good size and speed for the position. He can get to the next level in a hurry and uses his athleticism well. He will drop some passes, though, having 14 drops in 28 games.
20.outlook: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice (knee) has had a difficult time staying on the field in recent seasons. After missing 13 games in 2024 with a knee injury, he opened the 2025 season by serving a six-game suspension for his role in a hit-and-run incident. Rice then ended the 2025 season on Injured Reserve with a concussion. This past offseason has been eventful as well, as the 26-year-old underwent knee surgery in May before being arrested and serving a 30-day jail sentence for violating his probation. Rice is expected to be ready to go for the start of training camp, but his fantasy profile is obviously riddled with both injury and off-field risk. Across the eight games he suited up for in 2025, Rice recorded 53 catches for 571 yards and five touchdowns on 78 targets. As long as he's on the field, Rice projects as the number one option in the passing game for Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes. Particularly in PPR-scoring formats, Rice's upside is significant. However, fantasy managers will have to weigh his availability concerns when choosing whether to rely on him as a key contributor. All in all, Rice projects as a high-ceiling, low-floor fantasy WR3 entering 2026.

21.name: DeVonta Smith
21.comment: Smith was a little more up and down in an Eagles offense that struggled throwing the ball at times last season, but still managed to finish 19th overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He hit the 1,000-yard mark for the third time in four seasons. Smith had seven games with 14-plus fantasy points. The Eagles have a new offensive coordinator, hoping to find more consistency with the passing game. This could be a positive for Smith. He should be a top target in the offense once again, especially with A.J. Brown gone. Smith is a pretty complete receiver. He is a top route runner with great speed. He is a playmaker with the ball in his hands. Smith can do it all, being one of the top overall receivers in football. And he rarely drops a pass, dropping just 20 in five seasons.
21.outlook: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver DeVonta Smith is poised to enjoy a career season in 2026 following the departure of A.J. Brown. Throughout his career, Smith has operated as the primary No. 2 option in a run-heavy offense, with Brown seeing the majority of the targets from Jalen Hurts. However, with Brown now in New England, Smith is slated to operate as the clear WR1 in this offense, with first-round rookie Makai Lemon slated to slide in as the No. 2 option. Despite often sharing targets with Brown, Smith has still been very productive for fantasy finish as the overall WR20 in PPR scoring last season and the WR27 the year prior. In 2025, Smith saw 113 targets and brought in 77 of them for 1,008 yards and four touchdowns. Even though his touchdown total was the lowest of his career, this was Smith's second-highest target total of his career and third time over his last four seasons in which he exceeded the 1,000-yard mark in a season. The former Alabama standout has remained an elite option for Hurts downfield, as he has brought in at least 14 receptions of 20+ yards in each of his five NFL seasons and at least four passes for 40+ yards in three of his last four. Given that Brown saw 121 targets in 2025, Smith could be in store for a career-high in usage, even with Lemon joining the offense and the team resigning tight end Dallas Goedert. Even if Hurts and the Eagles lean on their rushing attack (11th-most rushing attempts in 2025), his high projected target share makes him worthy of a selection at his current Sleeper ADP of 49.0 (WR23). Managers should expect his ADP to continue to steadily climb over the summer.

22.name: Ladd McConkey
22.comment: McConkey had a bit of a disappointing year two, seeing his numbers take a dip. Much of this was because of the addition of Keenan Allen, who took away a lot of the targets McConkey saw his rookie season. McConkey was just 29th overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He had an uneven season, posting huge numbers one week while disappearing in others. McConkey had three games with 20-plus fantasy points. The Chargers new offense under Mike McDaniels could be a great fit for McConkey this year. He could rack up the targets in this scheme. McConkey is a great route runner with plus hands. He does well on all three levels and is a pretty complete receiver for a young player. He does lack a little strength and can have a some drop issues (11 in two seasons).
22.outlook: Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Ladd McConkey failed to build on his 1,149-yard, seven-touchdown rookie season in 2025, but the offensive changes taking place around him could make him a tremendous value entering year three. Under former offensive coordinator Greg Roman, the Chargers deployed three or more wide receivers on over 80% of their dropbacks, creating a crowded target environment that prevented any pass catcher from reaching 800 receiving yards. New offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel arrives from Miami, bringing with him 2025's third-most-utilized fullback, Alec Ingold. Los Angeles also aggressively pursued and signed tight end Charlie Kolar in free agency and later added David Njoku, strongly hinting at a shift toward more heavy personnel packages and two-receiver sets. With veteran Keenan Allen no longer on the roster, McConkey is positioned to claim one of those starting roles, and his skill set mirrors many of the traits that allowed Jaylen Waddle to thrive under McDaniel in Miami. Unlike Waddle, he ran fewer than 10% of his routes out of two-receiver sets last season. A shift toward heavier formations could dramatically increase that number and raise his route volume and target share in an offense that should see massive improvements under a more creative playcaller and with a healthier offensive line. Valued as RotoBaller's WR20, McConkey has a realistic path back to a WR1 finish at a discounted WR2 price.

23.name: Tee Higgins
23.comment: Higgins managed to finish 15th overall in fantasy receiver scoring despite not playing a full season and missing his quarterback for some of the year. He had a career-high 11 touchdowns, leading to his big fantasy production. He had three games with 20-plus fantasy points. Higgins has been a top-20 fantasy receiver four of five seasons. He starts opposite Ja'Marr Chase in one of the top offenses in football. Higgins has two 1,000-yard seasons for his career. Higgins is a very tall receiver with great athletic ability. He can really jump, making him an asset in the red zone and on deep throws. He does lack a little top-end speed but makes up for that with his other big-time abilities. And he does struggle some with drops at times, but has improved on that in recent years.
23.outlook: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins has battled injuries throughout the majority of his career, but when on the field, the Clemson product produced at an elite level. Across 15 games last season, Higgins found the back of the end zone an impressive 11 times and brought in 59 of his 98 targets for 846 yards. This stat line made him the WR15 in total PPR scoring, despite missing time. During the 2024 campaign, Higgins was just as dominant, bringing 10 touchdowns and 911 yards on 73 receptions over just 12 games. However, while the 27-year-old has missed ample time in his career, his quarterback, Joe Burrow, is also no stranger to the injured reserve. Burrow played in just eight games last season and only 10 in 2023, with his 2024 season serving as his only full 17-game season since the early stages of his career. When Burrow is on the field, Higgins is able to produce as a low-end WR1 despite sharing the field with superstar Ja'Marr Chase, given the team's massive passing volume. Since the Bengals are often trailing in games and have a subpar defense (third-most PPG allowed in 2025, eighth-most PPG allowed in 2024), the offense is forced to push the ball downfield. In the offseason, the Bengals did not make many major additions on defense and even lost superstar edge rusher Trey Hendrickson. Even though Higgins is the WR2 to one of the best pass catchers in the game, the 27-year-old is well-positioned to provide great value at his current 32.0 Sleeper ADP (WR14) in PPR drafts as he could finish as a borderline top-12 WR if Burrow can stay on the field.

24.name: Michael Wilson
24.comment: Wilson took his game to a new level last season, getting a chance to be the go-to target in the Cardinals passing game. Wilson had a 1,000-yard season despite starting just 13 of 17 games. He was 11th overall in fantasy receiver scoring. Wilson was a league winner for fantasy teams the second half of the season, having at least 13 fantasy points seven of his last eight games. He had four games during that stretch with 20-plus points. Wilson should continue to play a big role in the Cardinals offense going forward and could be the top receiver even with a healthy Marvin Harrison around. Wilson had just a drop all season despite getting targeted 126 times. Wilson has top speed for the position and is a good blocker at receiver. He could shore up his route running a little to become a more complete receiver but really made strides in that area last season.
24.outlook: Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Michael Wilson enters 2026 as a flex-range target after a productive third season. Wilson played 17 games and started 13 in 2025, catching 78 of 126 targets for 1,006 yards and seven touchdowns while averaging 12.9 yards per reception. He became the first Cardinals wide receiver to top 1,000 receiving yards since DeAndre Hopkins in 2020, and his 15-catch, 185-yard performance against San Francisco in Week 11 showed his ceiling when given volume. The concern is that much of Wilson's late-season surge came while Marvin Harrison Jr. was dealing with injuries, making it difficult to treat that production as a clean 2026 baseline. Arizona still has star tight end Trey McBride as a dominant target earner, Harrison remains the projected WR1 if healthy, and Kendrick Bourne adds another veteran option from the slot. The Cardinals also moved on from Kyler Murray, with Jacoby Brissett the likely bridge starter, with Gardner Minshew II and rookie Carson Beck also in the room. Arizona also hired former Rams OC Mike LaFleur to be the team's new head coach. According to LaFleur, Wilson will play "closer to the core" in the Puka Nacua role as the Z receiver in 2026, while Harrison will play the Davante Adams role as the X receiver. Wilson is currently being drafted as the WR34 on Sleeper, while RotoBaller ranks him 78th overall and WR37. That cost is manageable, but Wilson needs steady volume to become more than a volatile WR3 or FLEX option.

25.name: Jameson Williams
25.comment: Williams took another step forward last year, reaching the 1,000-yard mark for the second straight season. He was 10th overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He set more career highs in receptions (65) and yards (1,117). Williams had 10 of 17 games with double-digit fantasy points, showing a lot more consistency. He was a more well-rounded receiver last season. Remember, he is just 25 years old and still learning the position. He can still grow as a player. Williams seems to be just scratching the surface of what he can do. Expect him to play a similar role in the Lions explosive offense once again. Williams has game-changing speed and big-play ability. Williams might be one of the top home-run threats in the game. He needs some work on his route running but was much better in that area last season.
25.outlook: Detroit Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams got off to a slow start to the 2025 season, recording just 17 receptions for 289 yards and two touchdowns on 30 targets through the first eight weeks of the year. However, the 25-year-old's production picked up in a big way in the second half, and he finished the year with 65 catches for 1,117 yards and seven touchdowns on 102 targets across 17 games. The shift in Williams' fortunes largely coincided with a season-ending back injury for Lions tight end Sam LaPorta (back), who missed Detroit's final eight games. LaPorta is expected to be ready for the start of the 2026 season, which could impact Williams' target volume outlook. When the Lions have LaPorta, wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown, and running back Jahmyr Gibbs available, the team has traditionally utilized Williams in a downfield role. While his big-play ability gives him monster upside, Williams is also liable to finish fourth on his team in targets in any given week. Williams profiles as a boom/bust WR2 for fantasy managers heading into 2026.

26.name: Rome Odunze
26.comment: A foot injury limited Odunze to 12 games last year. He was on his way to a career-best season in year two before hurting his foot. He finished with 44 receptions for 661 yards and six touchdowns. Odunze was 40th overall in fantasy receiver scoring, having 15-plus fantasy points six games. Odunze could be setup for more targets this year with D.J. Moore gone. Odunze should start alongside Luther Burden, forming a top one-two punch in the Bears passing game. Odunze is a big, strong receiver that does well on the contested catch. He is a top playmaker at the position. His route running could sharpen some, though, before he becomes a complete NFL receiver.
26.outlook: After an up-and-down rookie campaign, Chicago Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze came out with a blazing start to the 2025 season, scoring five touchdowns in his first four games and going into the Bears' early bye week as the WR3 in Half-PPR formats. Coming out of the bye, the 2024 ninth overall pick started showing up on the injury report with foot and ankle issues, and while he continued to play through the nagging injuries, his production dropped, and he was eventually shut down for the final five games after being diagnosed with a stress fracture in his foot. Despite playing in only 12 games, Odunze's 87 targets led a talented group of Chicago pass catchers, and his six receiving touchdowns tied for the team lead. By year's end, five different Chicago players saw at least 60 targets, but with DJ Moore and Olamide Zaccheaus no longer on the team, Ben Johnson's passing offense is expected to funnel through Odunze, Luther Burden III, and Colston Loveland in 2026. With the thinning of the receiver room likely to produce an uptick in targets, and quarterback Caleb Williams expected to take a step forward in his second season with Johnson, Odunze has a chance to produce WR1 numbers from the mid-round range of drafts. In 2025, only Michael Penix Jr. and J.J. McCarthy had a higher off-target throw percentage than Williams, and no receiver was impacted more than Odunze. Williams completed at least 60% of his passes in only six games, and on the four such occurrences when Odunze was active, the second-year receiver averaged 18.4 fantasy points per game. When the connection is working, Odunze is capable of winning weeks, and at RotoBaller's WR36, that upside can still be had for a bargain in 2026.

27.name: Courtland Sutton
27.comment: Sutton had another good season as the No. 1 receiver for the Broncos. He had his second straight 1,000-yard season and was 12th overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He has been top 15 each of the last two years. Sutton had 11 of 17 games with double-digit fantasy points. Sutton should be the top target for this emerging offense once again. Sutton had fewer than 830 yards four straight seasons before the last two years. A consistent quarterback sure has made a difference for him. Sutton has a great combination of size and speed. He does a good job of making the catch above the defenders. He is a tall, strong target. He still lacks a little polish, but has made strides since entering the league. And drops can be a bit of an issue, having 17 his last two season.
27.outlook: Denver Broncos wide receiver Courtland Sutton put together another rock-solid season in 2025, hauling in 74 receptions for 1,017 yards and seven touchdowns on 124 targets across 17 games. Sutton has been extremely consistent in recent years, collecting just under 2,900 receiving yards and 25 touchdown catches since the start of 2023. However, Sutton could be in line for a reduced role in Denver this season after the team's offseason acquisition of former Miami Dolphins wideout Jaylen Waddle. With Waddle in town, Sutton's current streak of five consecutive seasons as the Broncos' lead target-earner appears to be in jeopardy. Denver also has a pair of up-and-coming wideouts in Pat Bryant and Troy Franklin, both of whom could be utilized to reduce Sutton's workload as he enters his age-31 season. Sutton's reliability in the red zone should give him a safe floor as a flex option, but he no longer projects as a top-24 wide receiver entering 2026.

28.name: Chris Godwin
28.comment: It took some time for Godwin to finally hit the field last year but ended up playing about half the games. He wasn't quite himself but got going eventually, finishing with 33 receptions for 360 yards and two touchdowns. Godwin hit double-digit fantasy points four of his last six games. He got healthier and started to look more like his self late in the year. With Mike Evans gone, Godwin has a chance to be the top target in this offense. Godwin had three straight 1,000-yard seasons before his last two injury-plagued seasons. Godwin is a big-play threat at receiver but has turned into a top-notch possession receiver in recent seasons. He has top speed and a knack for running by defenders. His route running and hands are much improved since earlier in his career, moving into the elite category of NFL receivers. Injuries have become a concern after the last two seasons.
28.outlook: Godwin is a bit of a question mark because of the last two years but he can be huge in this offense as long as he is healthy. Consider him a top No. 2 fantasy receiver because of the injury concern. Look for around 90 receptions for 1,100 yards and seven touchdowns.

29.name: Terry McLaurin
29.comment: McLaurin had a quad injury that limited him to 10 games last year. He had a decent season when on the field, having five games with double-digit fantasy points. McLaurin had 38 receptions for 582 yards and three touchdowns, finishing 55th overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He had five straight 1,000-yard seasons before last year. It was really the first season of his career that he battled injury. McLaurin will continue to be the top target for Jayden Daniels and the Commanders explosive offense. He is getting older, turning 31 shortly after the season starts. McLaurin is a speedy player that runs good routes and can make plays after the catch. He has good hands and a knack for making the clutch play. He is one of the top all-around receivers in the game.
29.outlook: McLaurin is getting older, so he might not be the elite fantasy receiver of past years. Consider him more of a No. 2 fantasy receiver. McLaurin can get around 80 receptions for 1,000 yards and seven touchdowns.

30.name: Brian Thomas Jr.
30.comment: Thomas didn't have quite the second season he hoped. He had some big games but was a little more inconsistent, especially if you consider the Jaguars passing game took a big step forward last year. He had 48 receptions for 707 yards and just three total touchdowns. Thomas had just five games all year with double-digit fantasy points. This was after a season Thomas topped 1,200-receiving yards and double-digit touchdowns. The Jaguars have more to compete with at receiver for targets but Thomas is expected to play a big role for the team. He should be the No. 1 receiver despite what happened last year. Thomas remains a huge talent. Thomas is a great athlete that can get to the next level in a hurry. He does well on the deep ball but can also turn a short pass into a big play. His route running needs a little work and drops are a concern after having 10 last year.
30.outlook: Thomas seems like a good buy-low candidate. He is too talented to struggle with consistency in this offense. Take him as a No. 2 and hope for a big rebound. Thomas can get around 80 receptions for 1,200 yards and nine touchdowns.

31.name: Jaylen Waddle
31.comment: Waddle was the No. 1 receiver for the Dolphins most of last year with Tyreek Hill getting hurt. Waddle did not have a huge season but produced some decent numbers in the Dolphins erratic offense. He had 64 receptions for 910 yards and six touchdowns. Waddle was 23rd overall in fantasy receiver scoring despite failing to reach 1,000 yards. He had a few big games, topping 20 fantasy points two times. Waddle had three straight 1,000-yard seasons to start his career but failed to hit that mark each of the past two years. He gets a fresh start with the Broncos this year, getting traded to Denver in the offseason. He will start opposite Courtland Sutton. Waddle might end up the top targets in this offense before all is said and done. Waddle has game-changing speed and can turn a short pass into a big play. He runs good routes and can get by defenders in a hurry. He lacks a little size, which causes some injury concerns.
31.outlook: Waddle is a bit of a wild card this year because you just aren't sure how he will be used in the offense. But he has a chance to emerge as the go-to target for Bo Nix, so a rebound is very possible. Take him as a No. 2 fantasy receiver. Look for around 80 receptions for 1,100 yards and seven touchdowns.

32.name: Alec Pierce
32.comment: Pierce took his game to a new level, benefiting from more consistent quarterback play. He had his first 1,000-yard season as a pro and led the league in yards per reception (21.3). He has led the league in yards per reception two straight seasons. He had nine of 15 games with double-digit fantasy points. Pierce signed a huge contract to remain with the Colts after the season and seems likely to be their No. 1 after the team traded Michael Pittman. Pierce has two straight seasons with 800-plus receiving yards. Pierce is a very physical receiver that uses his size and strength to his advantage. He isn't a polished route runner but can help make up for that because of his physical attributes. Pierce also can stretch the field because of his speed and strength. He can do a little bit of everything.
32.outlook: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Alec Pierce (ankle) put together the most productive season of his career in 2025, recording 47 receptions for 1,003 yards and six touchdowns on 84 targets across 15 games. The Colts rewarded the 26-year-old for his efforts in the offseason, re-signing him to a monster four-year, $114 million contract with $60 million guaranteed at signing. Pierce underwent offseason ankle surgery, but he's expected to be ready to go for the start of 2026. The Colts may also be planning for Pierce to step into the team's WR1 role, as Indianapolis traded away former top wideout Michael Pittman Jr. to the Pittsburgh Steelers in March. Pierce's best attribute as a pass-catcher remains his downfield ability, as he has led the NFL in yards per reception in each of the past two seasons. While his reliance on the deep ball creates volatility for his fantasy production, Pierce showed signs of becoming a more well-rounded receiver in his first season working with Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in 2025 by averaging a career-best 5.6 targets per game. If Pierce's usage continues to climb and he remains an explosive big-play threat, he could be in line for a breakout season in 2026. At the same time, Pierce's boom/bust track record creates uncertainty in his fantasy profile, particularly in PPR-scoring formats. All in all, Pierce projects as a high-risk, high-reward WR3 heading into 2026.

33.name: Carnell Tate
33.comment: The Titans picked Tate with the fourth selection in this year's draft. Tate has a chance to be the No. 1 receiver for the Titans from day one. He has good size and speed for the position and catches nearly everything thrown his way. Tate is a very good route runner for a young player. He can do well on the deep ball or turn a short pass into a big play. He does lack a little strength, though, and could bulk up some to compete better in the NFL.
33.outlook: Tennessee Titans wide receiver Carnell Tate was selected with the No. 4 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, demonstrating the team's belief that he can be a true No. 1 pass-catcher at the next level. Over the last half-decade, we've seen no shortage of wide receivers make immediate impacts, and Tate's primary competition for targets is a combination of Wan'Dale Robinson, Calvin Ridley, Chimere Dike, and Gunnar Helm. While Tate's floor and ceiling are dependent on Cam Ward's development in Year 2, the Ohio State product has all the skills and traits to be a fantasy football contributor in his rookie campaign. While sharing the field with Emeka Egbuka (2024) and Jeremiah Smith (2024-2025), Tate tallied 103 receptions for 1,608 yards and 13 touchdowns across 26 games over the last two seasons. Expect offensive coordinator Brian Daboll to force-feed the 21-year-old as early as the first game of his NFL career. He offers plenty of upside outside the top 50 overall picks in half-PPR setups.

34.name: D.K. Metcalf
34.comment: Metcalf was a little up and down his first season with the Steelers. He played in an offense that didn't take many chances down the field, though, which did not play to his strengths. Metcalf had an ADOT of 10.5, which was the lowest of his career. He was 25th overall in fantasy receiver scoring. Metcalf had nine of 15 games with double-digit fantasy points, including two games with 20-plus points. He will continue to serve as the top target in the Steelers offense. Metcalf has 1,000-yard seasons three of six. Metcalf is a big, strong receiver with speed, making him a very tough cover. He will drop some passes (at least seven drops four of seven seasons), though, and his route running isn't that of some of the other elite receivers. Regardless, Metcalf is a big-time talent and can make plays all over the field because of his abilities.
34.outlook: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf has failed to return ADP value in each of the past two seasons. Most recently, in his first year with the Steelers, he finished as the WR26 after coming off the board around WR20. Heading into 2026 as RotoBaller's WR35, he could still struggle to reverse that trend even at the lowest ADP since his 2019 rookie season. In 2025, Metcalf was the most persistent deep threat in a passing offense that lived largely in the short to intermediate areas of the field. At 42 years old, Aaron Rodgers ranked dead last among 33 qualified quarterbacks on intended air yards per attempt, finishing 1.6 yards below the league average. With Rodgers back in the fold for his 22nd and final professional season and the Steelers spending the offseason surrounding him with low-ADoT targets such as Michael Pittman Jr. and second-round pick Germie Bernard, there is no reason to expect a more aggressive downfield approach in 2026. In addition to adding more target competition, a philosophical shift to the Steelers' offense could create further obstacles to Metcalf's fantasy success. With Arthur Smith still running the offense in 2025, only the Baltimore Ravens deployed three-receiver sets at a lower rate, which allowed Metcalf to reach a 33.5% first-read target share. With new head coach Mike McCarthy having last run a Dallas offense operating out of 11-personnel on more than 70% of their 2024 snaps, both Pittman and Bernard are likely to be on the field regularly, earning targets. Metcalf is still the most naturally talented receiver on the roster, but in an environment not necessarily set up to take advantage of his skill set, he's fallen into the seventh round of 2026 drafts, and even at that range, the upside case is surprisingly difficult to make for a 6'4", 229-pound receiver who has three times topped 1,000 yards in a season.

35.name: Davante Adams
35.comment: Adams had a big first season with the Rams, leading the league in receiving touchdowns (14). He was ninth overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He even missed the last three games of the season. Adams did fail to reach 1,000 yards for the first time since 2019. He had five games with 20-plus fantasy points, having four games with multiple touchdowns. Adams will continue to start and be a big part of the Rams high-powered offense. Adams is getting older but hasn't lost much in recent seasons. Adams is a big, athletic target that does a good job of making the tough catch. He also has good hands, getting over some drop issues from earlier in his career. Adams has good speed and runs top routes.
35.outlook: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Davante Adams remains a high-upside fantasy option after catching 60 of 114 targets for 789 yards and an NFL-leading 14 touchdowns across 14 games in 2025. He finished as the WR9 in PPR formats while averaging 15.9 fantasy points per game, giving fantasy managers strong weekly production when healthy. Adams still carries clear value in Sean McVay's offense as a trusted scoring weapon for Matthew Stafford, especially with Puka Nacua drawing defensive attention on the other side. The concern is that Adams' production leaned heavily on touchdowns, with 84 of his 222.9 PPR points coming from scores. His 52.6% catch rate, limited yards-after-catch production (2.0), and late-season hamstring issue add real volatility entering 2026. Adams can still deliver spike weeks in a high-end offense, but the floor is not as safe as the name suggests. All the key pieces for the Rams are returning in Stafford, Nacua, and running backs Kyren Williams and Blake Corum, so Adams' role in the Rams offense shouldn't change much in 2026. He is currently going 43 overall as the WR19 on Sleeper, which sits well ahead of his WR18 ranking at RotoBaller, making him a risky bet at cost rather than a priority target.

36.name: Mike Evans
36.comment: Evans had injury issues for the first time in his career last season, playing eight games. He had double-digit fantasy points six of those games, though, producing well as usual. He had 30 receptions for 368 yards and three touchdowns. Evans had 11 straight 1,000-yard seasons before last year. He heads to the 49ers this year, playing for a different team for the first time in his career. Evans should slide right into a starting role for his new team. Evans is 32 years old and coming off an injury-plagued season, which is a concern. He averaged a career-worst 12.3 yards per reception last year, showing some signs of slowing down. Evans is a huge target with an enormous wing span. He does a fabulous job of catching the back-shoulder fade. He remains one of the best red-zone targets in the game. His size and strength makes him a very tough cover in the passing game. He does lack that elite speed, but it hasn't hampered much throughout his career.
36.outlook: After spending the first 12 years of his NFL career with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, veteran wide receiver Mike Evans is entering his first season with the San Francisco 49ers in 2026. Evans battled through an injury-marred campaign in 2025, missing nine games with hamstring and collarbone issues and finishing the season with 30 receptions for 368 yards and three touchdowns on 62 targets. However, the 32-year-old has a long history as one of the most consistent wide receivers in the NFL, averaging 74 receptions, 1,084 receiving yards, and 11 touchdowns per season between 2020 and 2024. Evans should have a chance to reclaim his status as a lead wide receiver in San Francisco following the offseason departures of former 49ers wideouts Jauan Jennings and Brandon Aiyuk. While the 49ers have a pair of high-volume target earners in running back Christian McCaffrey and tight end George Kittle, Evans brings a different element to the team's offense as a true X receiver on the outside. Given his injury issues in 2025 and his age, Evans' profile is not without risk for fantasy managers. Still, his ability to make plays down the field and in the red zone should provide him with a stable production floor, particularly in a strong offensive environment in San Francisco. All in all, Evans projects as a low-end WR2/high-end WR3 entering 2026.

37.name: Marvin Harrison Jr.
37.comment: Harrison had some injury issues last year, missing five games, but was a little disappointing when on the field. He had 41 receptions for 608 yards and four touchdowns. Harrison finished with double-digit fantasy points six times. He failed to have a 100-yard game all season. Harrison ended up watching Michael Wilson emerge as the go-to target for the Cardinals while he was sidelined. A new coaching staff could be a positive for Harrison, who could help him finally reach his potential. It hasn't happened to date. Harrison is not a speed burner but runs top routes and knows how to get open. He plays faster than his timed speed. Harrison can struggle some against press coverage and will drop some passes at times (nine in two seasons).
37.outlook: Since being selected fourth overall in the 2024 NFL Draft, Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. has struggled to live up to the hype he received as a prospect. The 23-year-old ran into a string of poor injury luck in 2025, suffering a concussion and missing time due to appendicitis before finally being placed on season-ending Injured Reserve with heel and foot issues. Still, Harrison Jr. was not particularly effective when on the field, recording 41 receptions for 608 yards and four touchdowns on 73 targets across 12 games. By the time he went out for the year, Harrison Jr. had fallen to the number three target in Arizona behind superstar tight end Trey McBride and breakout wide receiver Michael Wilson. The Cardinals overhauled their coaching staff over the offseason, which could help provide Harrison Jr. with a much-needed fresh start. However, the young wideout admitted during OTAs that he's still feeling the effects of last season's injuries. While Harrison Jr. also said he did not think the injury issues will linger into the regular season, the fact that he might not be fully healthy entering a critical training camp is a bit alarming. Harrison Jr. remains a high-upside wide receiver and could be a worthy buy-low target for fantasy managers, but he should be viewed as a boom/bust WR3/flex option in redraft formats heading into 2026.

38.name: Parker Washington
38.comment: Washington had a breakout third season, emerging as a starter and clear top target in the Jaguars improved passing game. He was 26th overall in fantasy receiver scoring, finishing with 58 receptions for 847 yards and five touchdowns. He has 19-plus fantasy points three straight games to end his season. Washington had double-digit fantasy points eight of 16 games. Washington has a lot to compete with for targets but should get his work, proving to be a top option last year. Plus, quarterback Trevor Lawrence seems to have a good rapport with him. Washington knows how to get open and catches the ball well. He lacks a little speed but that hasn't held him back much. He has a knack for making the big play as evident by his 14.6 yards per reception last year. He did have some drop issues last season, dropping seven passes after having just two his first two years.
38.outlook: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington's league-winning finish to the 2025 season is not being reflected in his current draft cost, making him a potential steal in the middle rounds of 2026 drafts. Washington led the Jaguars in targets, receptions, and receiving yards, and he was arguably the largest factor in Trevor Lawrence's QB1 pace over the final 10 weeks of the season. From Weeks 9 through 18, Washington caught 41 passes for 640 yards and came down with four of his career-high five touchdown grabs. His 12.6 Half-PPR points per game were good enough to make him the WR11 over that stretch, and in Jacksonville's Wild Card loss to the Bills, Washington again led the team with seven catches for 107 yards and a touchdown. His RotoBaller ranking of WR33 heading into drafts puts him in the same mid-round range as teammates Brian Thomas Jr. and Jakobi Meyers, with whom he is expected to split the bulk of Lawrence's targets in 2026. With all three proving to be capable WR1s at varying points throughout the past two seasons, and with the presence of 2025 second overall pick Travis Hunter looming as additional target competition, uncertainty about Jacksonville's exact pecking order has pushed down the value of the entire room. With none of them coming off the board until the sixth round or later in single-quarterback drafts, it's likely that at least one, and potentially all three, will drastically outperform ADP, and with Washington proving himself to be Lawrence's most trusted target down the stretch, he's as safe a bet as any to emerge as the team's most valuable fantasy receiver.

39.name: Jordyn Tyson
39.comment: Many considered Tyson the most talented receiver in this year's drat. He was the second receiver off the board, getting picked by the Saints with the eighth overall pick. Tyson should move into a starting role immediately, playing opposite Chris Olave. Tyson could become the top target on the team in a hurry. He has good size and strength for the position. He is very good on the contested catch and can get in and out of his breaks in a hurry. He is a much improved route runner from earlier in his college career but still has room to grow in that area. Injuries were an issue his last year in college, which is a bit of a concern.
39.outlook: New Orleans Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson was the No. 8 overall selection in the 2026 NFL Draft after producing 136 receptions for 1,812 yards and 18 touchdowns in 21 games over the last two seasons at Arizona State.
