Injuries have been an issue for the 21-year-old, as he played in just three games in 2023, missed the Big 12 Championship and College Football Playoff in 2024, and sat out three games in 2025. But when he has been available, he's been dominant. Despite his injury concerns, the Saints were comfortable enough with his medicals to take him in the top 10. Now, he joins an offense alongside Chris Olave, catching passes from Tyler Shough, who had a quietly solid rookie campaign in 2025. In Year 1 under the head coach Kellen Moore, the Saints were eighth in passing attempts per game (26.7), a common theme for Moore dating back to his tenure with the Dallas Cowboys and Los Angeles Chargers. With Olave drawing coverage in the middle of the field, there is room for Tyson to have a productive rookie season, making him an enticing selection at his late-sixth-round ADP in half-PPR setups.

40.name: Jakobi Meyers
40.comment: A move to Jacksonville was a great one for Meyers last year. He had 42 receptions for 483 yards and two touchdowns in nine games with the Jaguars. If he plays a full season with Jacksonville, he has 79 receptions for 912 yards and six touchdowns. Meyers had five games with double-digit fantasy points for the Jaguars. He will continue to start in the Jaguars suddenly high-powered passing game and be a top target in this offense. Meyers has topped 800 yards five straight seasons. He is not a top athlete, but knows his limitations and does well with his ability. Meyers runs good routes and has solid hands, dropping just 18 passes his entire career.
40.outlook: The Jacksonville Jaguars acquired wide receiver Jakobi Meyers from the Las Vegas Raiders at last season's trade deadline and saw immediate returns. Meyers made his team debut in a Week 10 loss to the Houston Texans before Jacksonville closed the 2025 regular season on an eight-game winning streak. Quarterback Trevor Lawrence also enjoyed arguably the best stretch of his career after Meyers arrived, producing as the fantasy QB1 from Week 10 on with 2,100 passing yards and 25 total touchdowns. During that same span, Meyers posted WR18 fantasy numbers by hauling in 42 receptions for 483 yards and three scores. Still, it's fair to question Meyers' role entering 2026 as a member of one of the NFL's most intriguing receiver corps. Parker Washington broke out late last season and carried that momentum into Jacksonville's playoff appearance, while Brian Thomas Jr. endured a disappointing follow-up to his elite rookie campaign. Then there's Travis Hunter (knee), who is expected to be healthy for training camp but is far from guaranteed to serve as a focal point offensively and could even see an increased defensive workload in his second season. Despite the uncertainty surrounding Jacksonville's pass catchers, Meyers has one clear advantage: financial investment. The Jaguars signed the 29-year-old to a three-year, $60 million extension that includes $40 million guaranteed, making him one of the league's 25 highest-paid receivers. With a full offseason to become more comfortable in Liam Coen's system, Meyers could surprise fantasy managers who draft him as a WR3 or flex option this year.

41.name: Jordan Addison
41.comment: Addison had his struggles last year in a Vikings passing game that really struggled. Addison had his worst season to date, finishing with 42 receptions for 610 yards and four total touchdowns. Addison was just 44th overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He had double-digit fantasy points seven of 14 games. Addison had two 100-yard games. Addison will continue to start opposite superstar receiver Justin Jefferson. A likely change at quarterback to Kyler Murray should be a big positive for Addison. Addison has never had a 1,000-yard season but has 850-plus yards two of three years. Addison has top speed for the position and does well on short and deep routes. He gets in and out of his breaks in a hurry. Addison will struggle a little with the contested catch but drops weren't a big issue his first three seasons, which is encouraging.
41.outlook: Although Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jordan Addison was not drafted nearly as early as Justin Jefferson in 2025 fantasy leagues, his managers were similarly impacted by the team's offensive struggles. Addison, who finished as a top-24 fantasy receiver in each of his first two seasons, averaged just over eight fantasy points per game while finishing as the WR44 across 14 contests last year, and scored just one touchdown with J.J. McCarthy at quarterback. The 24-year-old established himself as a legitimate red-zone threat during his first two NFL campaigns and could emerge as a strong bounce-back candidate if Kyler Murray is named the team's Week 1 starter. While the Vikings recently signed veteran receiver Jauan Jennings to a one-year deal, the former 49er is more likely to absorb the 53 targets vacated by Jalen Nailor's departure than threaten Addison's role as WR2. Fantasy managers should monitor Minnesota's quarterback situation closely this offseason while viewing Addison as a WR3 with significant upside.

42.name: Jayden Reed
42.comment: Reed broke his collarbone in Week 2 and missed much of the year, derailing his season. He failed to have more than 60 yards in a game. Reed had double-digit fantasy points two of seven games. He finished with 19 receptions for 207 yards and a touchdown. Reed had two straight seasons with 790-plus yards before last year. Reed is expected to play a big role in the Packers passing game this year, especially with the departure of Romeo Doubs. Reed doesn't really wow you in any one area, but is a solid all-around target. He runs good routes and does well on the contested catch. He also does well after the catch, showing good playmaking ability.
42.outlook: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Jayden Reed has one of the widest ranges of outcomes of all fantasy receivers heading into 2026. Since arriving in the league as a second-round pick in 2023, he has regularly flashed playmaking ability, but inconsistent usage has prevented him from developing into a reliable every-week fantasy starter. Now that significant changes are coming to Green Bay's offense, past history needs to be weighed against a potential snap-share bump. Green Bay will be without two of its leading receivers from 2025, having allowed Romeo Doubs to walk in free agency and trading away Dontayvion Wicks, but it's no foregone conclusion that the added opportunity will go Reed's way. The fresh recipient of a four-year, $92 million contract extension, fifth-year wideout Christian Watson appears locked into an every-down role, and when the Packers take a third receiver off the field, as they did at one of the league's highest rates in 2025, it could be 2025 first-round pick Matthew Golden who claims the opposite spot. Across three NFL seasons, Reed has run fewer than 10 of his nearly 900 routes from two-receiver sets, and with tight end Tucker Kraft reportedly trending toward an early-season return from his Week 9 ACL tear, there's no reason to expect a sudden influx of 11-personnel usage in Green Bay. Reed did sign a three-year extension of his own this offseason, and he offers intriguing upside thanks to his proven yards after catch ability and chemistry with Jordan Love, but without the certainty of an every-down role, he is still a risky pick before the mid-to-late rounds of 2026 drafts. At RotoBaller's WR43, he profiles as a boom-or-bust WR4 who continues to hold more value in best ball formats.

43.name: Christian Watson
43.comment: Watson missed the first six games of the season as he recovered from a torn ACL. He played pretty well when he finally found the field. He had 35 receptions for 611 yards and six touchdowns. Watson had five games with double-digit fantasy points, including three games with 20-plus points. Watson was a consistent factor as a starter for the Packers. He would have enjoyed a career season if he was able to play a full year. Watson has never topped 700-receiving yards and battled injuries each of his first four years. Watson will remain a big part of the Packers passing game. Watson is a tall receiver that can get downfield in a hurry. He can separate in a hurry and has top speed for the position. He lacks a little polish with his route running, though, and injuries have plagued him in four seasons.
43.outlook: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson is in a fantastic position to succeed in 2026. The Packers' wide receiver room is the least crowded it has been since Watson's rookie season. After jettisoning fellow wide receivers Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks, this team has stated its faith in Watson, Matthew Golden, and Jayden Reed. Watson is entering the 2026 season with some momentum. Despite only playing in 10 games in 2025, Watson fell just nine yards short of his career high in receiving yards. He also caught an impressive six touchdowns in those 10 games. His performance made him an effective contributor in fantasy. Additionally, Watson is on a prove-it deal in 2026. He signed a one-year $11 million contract extension last season, and we have seen many massive seasons over the years from players looking to secure a new contract. At the end of the day, Watson is going to be the No. 1 target in a good offense. He is perfectly positioned to record his first 1,000-yard season. As such, Watson is worth a shot around the eighth round in fantasy drafts.

44.name: Rashid Shaheed
44.comment: Shaheed started his season with the Saints but was dealt to the Seahawks, becoming the No. 3 receiver for his new team. He had better numbers with the Saints than Seahawks but still managed a career-high 59 receptions. Shaheed was 38th overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He had just two games reaching double-digit fantasy points with the Seahawks. Shaheed signed a big deal with the Seattle after the season to stay with the team and become the clear No. 2 for the team from day one. Shaheed is a top big-play threat at receiver. He averages a robust 14.7 yards per reception for his career. Shaheed has great speed for the position and can get down the field in a hurry. He is a top deep threat. His route running could use a little work but he made strides in that area last year.
44.outlook: Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Rashid Shaheed experienced two distinct chapters in 2025, totaling 59 catches for 687 yards and two receiving scores. However, 44-499-2 of that line came in nine games with the Saints, which was good for the WR31 in half-PPR formats. Seattle then scooped him in a trade, but his involvement was limited to 15 scoreless catches over the final nine contests. Shaheed's biggest impact with the Seahawks came as a returner, though that doesn't help most fantasy managers. The skill set that made him a WR3 on the Saints didn't suddenly evaporate. It is reasonable to think that Seattle, which gave him a three-year deal worth $51 million this offseason, has bigger plans now that they've had a year to integrate him into the system. Their rushing offense is also a bigger question mark with Zach Charbonnet recovering from knee surgery and Kenneth Walker III in Kansas City. While the defense can carry games, the offense should get more aerial as well. The speedster's RotoBaller rank around pick 145 is close to the summer 138 ADP (WR56), so there's room to profit for those who believe his role will expand.

45.name: Makai Lemon
45.comment: The Eagles picked Lemon with the 20th pick in this year's draft. Philadelphia hopes to have found their starter opposite DeVonta Smith for years to come. Lemon is a very talented pass catcher. He catchers nearly everything thrown his way and does well on the contested catch. He can do well at all three levels at receiver. He is a pretty good route runner but won't do a ton after the catch. Lemon also could add a little strength, so he won't get pushed around in coverage at the NFL level.
45.outlook: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Makai Lemon was the No. 20 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft following a 79-catch, 1,156-yard, 11-touchdown season for USC. He won the Fred Biletnikoff Award, given to college football's most outstanding wideout. He landed with one of the NFL's most successful franchises in recent history, but despite the expectation that A.J. Brown will be traded before the regular season, his ceiling could be limited in Philly's offense. Despite having four offensive coordinators over the last five seasons, the Eagles have yet to finish in the top 20 in pass rate. With Jalen Hurts, Saquon Barkley, and a strong offensive line back in play in 2026, that's unlikely to change, and the Eagles should have a great defense once again -- leading to a lack of passing volume. Combine these factors with Lemon having to compete with DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert, Marquise Brown, and Eli Stowers for targets and snaps from Day 1, and it could take time for him to become a consistent fantasy producer. There is a chance Lemon breaks out immediately and becomes Hurts' No. 1 target, but it's more likely that it'll take the duo some seasoning to get on the same page. Expect Lemon to post a few spike weeks as a rookie, but his seventh-round ADP makes him an expensive gamble based on his current outlook. His long-term outlook and ceiling exceed his redraft projection.

46.name: Romeo Doubs
46.comment: Doubs picked a good time to have his best season to date, catching 55 passes for 724 yards and six touchdowns. He was 36th overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He had seven games with double-digit fantasy points. Doubs dropped a career-low three passes despite getting targeted 85 times. Doubs turned his best season into a big contract with the Patriots. He will become a starter in the Patriots emerging passing game. Doubs has at least 40 receptions all four seasons in the NFL but never topped 750 yards in a season. Doubs has good speed and can stretch the field in a hurry. He is an improved route runner from earlier in his career. He lacks a little strength, though, getting pushed around in press coverage.
46.outlook: Romeo Doubs signed a four-year, $68 million contract with the New England Patriots this offseason. Doubs' time as New England's No. 1 wide receiver was short-lived when the Patriots acquired A.J. Brown from the Eagles in June. The 26-year-old is expected to play primarily out of the slot for the Patriots and should see more favorable matchups, as defenses will focus on shutting down Brown. Doubs never logged a 1,000-yard season or even a 100-yard game during the regular season in his tenure at Green Bay, but balled out when it mattered by averaging 123.7 receiving yards in four playoff games. The Patriots have a lot of success with receivers playing out of the slot and recently let go of Stefon Diggs, who racked up 1,103 yards and four touchdowns while lining up inside the slot 45-50% of the time last season. Doubs is set as New England's No. 2 wide receiver, but will compete with not only Brown, but Kayshon Boutte, Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, and Kyle Williams for targets. RotoBaller has Doubs ranked as WR53 and 122 overall, which aligns with his Sleeper ADP of 123. Coming off a massive contract, the Patriots will find ways to get Doubs the ball, but he is more of a weekly FLEX play given the competition for targets and the Pats' tougher schedule heading into 2026.

47.name: Josh Downs
47.comment: Downs saw a bit of a downturn in production with some other options emerging in the Colts passing game. He had career lows in receptions (58) and receiving yards (566). Downs was 42nd overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He was pretty consistent as the No. 3 receiver in the offense, having double-digit fantasy points eight of 16 games. Downs has a chance for a bigger role his year after the departure of Michael Pitttman. He could really rack up the targets vacated by Pittman. Downs has 68 or more receptions two of three seasons. Downs gets in and out of his breaks in a hurry. He has top speed at the position and makes a lot of plays after the catch. Downs is a top athlete. He does lack some size and can get pushed around in press coverage. He also has at least four drops each of his first three seasons.
47.outlook: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs came into the 2025 season as one of the most hyped breakout candidates in the league. While it was ultimately teammate Alec Pierce who would go on to win weeks as a late-round receiver pick out of Indianapolis, Downs ended the year as the WR48, the worst result of his career and a full 12 spots lower than his 2024 finish. With that kind of disappointment leaving a bad taste in the mouths of many drafters, Downs is severely underrated heading into 2026 drafts, despite having one of the best offseasons a receiver could ask for. Michael Pittman Jr., who led the team in targets in each of his past five seasons with the Colts, was traded to Pittsburgh in the early offseason, creating the opportunity for Downs to add to his 93-target and 66-reception averages across his first three years in the league. While he still profiles primarily as a slot receiver, Indianapolis no longer has the personnel to keep Downs off the field in two-receiver sets. The Colts did not select a pass-catcher until the seventh round of the NFL Draft, adding Deion Burks to a wide receiver room that currently has Nick Westbrook-Ikhine penciled into the third spot. Receiving work in Indianapolis is slated to run through Downs, Pierce, and tight end Tyler Warren in 2026, and as long as quarterback Daniel Jones does not miss extensive time after an Achilles tear ended his first season with the Colts, Downs should be a lock to return the type of late-round value that he could not in 2025. At RotoBaller's WR48, he is currently being drafted at his absolute floor.

48.name: Michael Pittman Jr.
48.comment: Pittman had another productive season as the top receiver in the Colts offense. He was 18th overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He had some big games, scoring 20-plus fantasy points four times. He had 80 receptions for 784 yards and seven touchdowns, setting a career-high in scores. Pittman was traded to the Steelers this offseason and will be their No. 2 receiver for the coming season. He should be the top possession target in this offense. Pittman has 80 or more receptions four of five seasons. Pittman is a big, tall receiver with good strength. He can do pretty well against press coverage and make the tough catch in coverage. He can do well as a possession receiver or on the deep ball. He is a well-rounded receiver in the prime of his career.
48.outlook: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. had 80 receptions on 111 targets for 784 yards and seven touchdowns in 2025. It was a new career high in touchdowns for Pittman, but it was his lowest yardage total since his rookie season in 2020. A prominent piece in the Colts' surprisingly dynamic offense during the first half of the season, Pittman's production fell off a cliff after his only 100-yard performance of the season in Week 9. From Week 10 on, Pittman averaged 27.9 receiving yards and 3.54 PPR points per game. Now playing opposite DK Metcalf in Pittsburgh, Pittman is no longer the default WR1 on his team, and his streak of five consecutive 100-target seasons may be at its end. On the bright side, Pittman's quarterback situation is the best it's ever been, as future Hall of Famer Aaron Rodgers is returning for another year with the Steelers. Even if their complementary playstyles benefit Pittman's volume, his inconsistent returns in favorable conditions over the years make it hard to believe that 2026 will be much different. Pittman is RotoBaller's WR42 in its current rankings.

49.name: Calvin Ridley
49.comment: Ridley had a disappointing season, getting limited to seven games because of injury. He showed some flashes when on the field, though, having 17 receptions for 303 yards. Ridley had a big Week 5, finishing with five receptions for 131 yards on 10 targets. He will look to get healthy this year and back to his big ways. Getting to work with offensive coordinator Brian Daboll should be a positive for Ridley. He had two straight 1,000-yard seasons before last year. Ridley does have Wan'Dale Robinson to compete with for targets this year. Ridley could be second fiddle to Robinson most weeks. Ridley is a pretty complete package at receiver. He can make plays after the catch, make a big play down the field, and has plus hands. He has very good speed and is a tough cover because of his ability to do well on shorter and deep routes.
49.outlook: Ridley is a bit of a wild card after last year. He has a high ceiling, though, based off past success. He could rebound and might be worth taking a chance on as a No. 3 fantasy receiver. He can get around 60 receptions for 900 yards and six touchdowns.

50.name: KC Concepcion
50.comment: The Browns added a much-needed weapon to their passing game, taking Concepcion with the 24th overall pick. He should move into a starting role for the team immediately. He is a big-time playmaker. He makes tons of plays after the catch and does well in getting open because of his quickness and route running. He can separate in a hurry. Concepcion will drop some passes and lacks a little elite speed.
50.outlook: Cleveland Browns wide receiver KC Concepcion was the No. 24 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft after a strong single season at Texas A&M. The New York native spent the first two seasons of his collegiate career at NC State before transferring to College Station. Overall, he tallied 185 receptions for 2,218 yards and 25 touchdowns in 38 games. He also averaged 6.2 yards per carry on 70 attempts and returned two punts for touchdowns. Concepcion is fast and twitchy, making him a splash-play specimen capable of making a big impact at the next level. His future outlook is bright, but his landing spot isn't ideal for his Year 1 production. In 2026, he'll be catching passes from Deshaun Watson and/or Shedeur Sanders while competing for targets with Harold Fannin Jr., Denzel Boston, and Jerry Jeudy. He's an interesting best ball dart throw thanks to his one-play-touchdown upside, but expectations for his rookie season, especially in non-PPR leagues, should be tempered. All that said, he's a viable early-season stash at his ADP well outside the top 120 picks in half-PPR setups.

51.name: Kayshon Boutte
51.comment: Boutte was a little boom or bust last year. He had some big games but disappeared in others. He had five games with double-digit fantasy points but seven others with less than five points. Boutte did top 550 yards for the second straight season. Boutte has a lot to compete with for targets in New England but has a chance to earn starting job. Boutte has a good combination of speed and size. He can get to the next level quickly, running by defenders. He also does well on turning a short pass into a big play. He will struggle some on shorter routes, failing to have a complete route tree just yet.
51.outlook: In 2025, New England Patriots receiver Kayshon Boutte posted his second consecutive respectable season. Boutte's volume declined noticeably to 33 receptions on 46 targets in 14 games, but he did well with those opportunities. Boutte had the fifth-highest aDOT of all receivers at 17.0 yards, leading to a league-best 12.0 yards per target as well as six touchdowns. His campaign culminated in a WR51 finish, and he was the WR47 on a per-game basis. It is unclear if Boutte will see even that diminished volume in 2026, though. New England acquired star receiver A.J. Brown from Philadelphia in early June, adding a new top option to the team's receiving room. Additionally, the Patriots signed Romeo Doubs to a four-year, $68 million deal in March. Boutte will be forced to compete with Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, and Kyle Williams, plus tight ends Hunter Henry and Eli Raridon, for scraps. Unless Boutte gets traded, that is, a possibility that has been rumored for a while. Boutte has been taken as the WR68 in fantasy drafts. The chance that he finds a new home with a clearer path to higher target volume makes him an intriguing bet at that price.

52.name: Xavier Worthy
52.comment: Worthy had his second kind of ho-hum season. Most thought he would take a huge step forward in year two, but that didn't happen. He was just 58th overall in fantasy receiver scoring, finishing with 42 receptions for 532 yards and a touchdown. He had double-digit fantasy points just five of 14 games. He reached double-digit points just one time after Week 8. His usage was up and down in this offense. Worthy is likely to play a similar role for the Chiefs this coming season. He will be used out of the slot and get some chances to carry the ball. Worthy is a speed burner. He can get to the next level in a hurry. The Chiefs will use him all over the field to take advantage of his playmaking ability. Worthy does lack some strength, though, and can get pushed around in coverage. He also can struggle some on contested catches.
52.outlook: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Xavier Worthy is looking to rebound after requiring offseason shoulder surgery to fully repair the torn labrum suffered in Week 1's collision with Travis Kelce. He wound up only missing two weeks, logging 42 total catches for 532 yards and one touchdown over 14 games. It's no surprise that his diminished effectiveness led to a lower deep-ball catch rate, and Worthy also failed to score on any of his three end-zone targets. One cannot forget that alongside Worthy's 59-638-6 rookie receiving line was another three rushing TDs on 20 carries (104 yards). While he still gained 87 yards on 11 rushes in '25, the TD variance was not in his favor. The Chiefs also struggled as a team, losing key players like Patrick Mahomes II, Rashee Rice, and Isiah Pacheco for stretches. And though Worthy was still rocking a no-contact jersey during OTAs as a precaution, all reports have been optimistic about his readiness for Week 1. With the offense seemingly approaching 100%, we can hope that Year 3 Worthy gets robust downfield usage to show off that health, speed, and separation. His June half-PPR ADP around pick 117 lags roughly 15 spots behind our RotoBaller rank, which makes him a solid dart throw for most flex slots.

53.name: Jerry Jeudy
53.comment: Jeudy had a terrible season, struggling with consistence in an offense that was pretty horrible all season long. He had just 602 yards after a career-best season. It was a step backwards for Jeudy. He struggled with consistency, dropping 10 passes. He has 23 drops his last two years and three season for his career with double-digit drops. Jeudy just hasn't lived up to his potential. He has more to complete with for targets this year with the Browns drafting two top receivers. Jeudy won't be handed anything but should at least be third on the depth chart. And maybe a more stable quarterback situation will get things turned around for him this year. Jeudy is a very good route runner with top speed. He catches the ball well and can make plays after the catch. He lacks a little size, though, and drops are clearly an issue.
53.outlook: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Jerry Jeudy was disappointing last season in a sputtering Browns offense. He finished with 50 catches for 602 yards and two touchdowns across 17 games. The situation surrounding Jeudy wasn't great, but the supporting cast doesn't account for all of Jeudy's struggles. The 27-year-old was targeted 106 times but also led the NFL in drops with nine and had an abysmal 47.2% catch rate. Cleveland's offense was at the bottom of the league last year and did Jeudy no favors last season after he racked up 1,229 receiving yards the year before. The Browns revamped their wide receiver room this offseason by drafting Texas A&M wideout KC Concepcion with the 24th pick and Washington wideout Denzel Boston with the 39th pick of the 2026 NFL Draft. Cedric Tillman and Isaiah Bond round out the rest of the Browns wide receiver room. Concepcion and Boston are legit options that could dethrone Jeudy as Cleveland's top wide receiver, and he will compete with emerging tight end Harold Fannin Jr. for targets. Jeudy's contract will keep him on the field. Still, it will be tough for him to surpass 1,000 receiving yards with additional competition for targets regardless of whether Deshaun Watson or Shedeur Sanders wins the Browns' starting quarterback job. RotoBaller projects Jeudy to catch 53 passes for 701 yards and four touchdowns in 2026. Jeudy is WR66 in the latest RotoBaller rankings, which aligns with Sleeper ADP of 179. The Browns offense should be better this year, and Jeudy is worth taking a late-round flier as Cleveland's No. 1 wide receiver in upcoming drafts.

54.name: Jalen Nailor
54.comment: Nailor had two very similar seasons his last two with theVikings. He had 29 receptions for 444 yards and three touchdowns last year after having 28 for 414 and six touchdowns the previous year. He has shown flashes of good things with his chances. He had two games last year with 19-plus fantasy points. The Raiders signed Nailor and will give him a chance to compete for a starting job with his new team. Nailor has great speed and can stretch the field in a hurry. He can serve as a top deep threat. Injuries can be a concern but he has played a full season each of his last two years.
54.outlook: Las Vegas Raiders wide receiver Jalen Nailor finally finds himself with a good chance at seeing consistent involvement on the field following four years as an ancillary piece in Minnesota. He only had 12 total catches between 21 games in 2022-23, but grew into a 57-858-10 receiving line across 34 games in 2024-25. He only topped 50 yards once in 2026, but he made it count, securing five catches for 124 yards and a score in Week 10. The Raiders will either be led by rookie Fernando Mendoza or veteran Kirk Cousins, neither of whom is a bankable asset. This is offset by Nailor joining a weak WR corps, where talent can readily make him the No. 1 WR, even if he'd still be behind TE Brock Bowers. There's offseason buzz saying that Nailor is going to be the Jaxon Smith-Njigba in Klint Kubiak's new LV offense. That's a 99th-percentile runout, but the point stands that there is little resistance to the opportunity. His WR61/Pick 160 ADP as of mid-June leaves plenty of room for profit.

55.name: Jauan Jennings
55.comment: Jennings started all of last season for the 49ers but didn't have quite the season he hoped. He had 55 receptions for 643 yards and nine touchdowns. His scores really helped his fantasy production, finishing 32nd overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He had eight games with 12-plus fantasy points. Jennings didn't quite take advantage of his playing time like the previous year. He should get a chance to start this season, but it won't be handed to him. Jennings is a very big receiver with good size and strength. He looks more like a tight end than a receiver. He will drop some passes (three seasons with five or more drops), and his route running still needs some sharpening.
55.outlook: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings will step in as the team's new WR3 after inking a one-year, $13 million deal in May. Stuck firmly behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison on the depth chart, he is not in an ideal situation to stage a rebound off a disappointing 2025 campaign with the San Francisco 49ers. In the wake of Deebo Samuel's departure and Brandon Aiyuk's contract drama, the stage was set for Jennings to emerge as the 49ers' alpha receiver. However, a litany of injuries cost Jennings two games, limited his involvement when active, and impaired his playmaking ability. He finished the season with 55 receptions, 643 yards, and nine touchdowns on 90 targets. The Vikings have a strong tendency to operate out of three-WR sets, so Jennings should still be on the field often, but with a greatly reduced target share. Jennings will be functioning more as a role player than a featured receiver with his new team, limiting his fantasy value in 2026. He is listed as the WR58 in RotoBaller's early rankings.

56.name: De'Zhaun Stribling
56.comment: The 49ers got Stribling with the first pick in the second round of this year's draft. He should play an immediate role with his new team, serving as the top deep threat at receiver. Stribling has elite speed and can really take the top off defenses. He should be a good compliment to starters Mike Evans and Ricky Pearsall. Stribling does have a bit of a limited route tree at this stage of his career. He is kind of a one-trick pony. He will make the acrobatic catch and is tough to bring down with the ball in his hands.
56.outlook: The San Francisco 49ers shocked the world with the first pick of the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft, taking Ole Miss receiver De'Zhaun Stribling. Standing 6-foot-2, Stribling had a productive college career that spanned three different schools over five seasons. His combination of size and speed made him an intriguing NFL prospect, and he landed in a great spot to make an early impact. He projects to be behind Mike Evans, Ricky Pearsall, and Christian Kirk on the depth chart as of now, but none of those three players has a clean history of staying healthy for a full season. An injury to one of those guys could get Stribling on the field in a Jauan Jennings-esque role, which has been productive for fantasy over the past few seasons.

57.name: Jalen Coker
57.comment: Coker emerged for the Panthers the second half of the season and was a big factor in the passing game, staring opposite Tet McMillan. He had double-digit fantasy points four of his last seven games. And he had his best game of the entire season in the playoffs, catching nine passes for 134 yards and a touchdown on 12 targets. Coker has a good chance to start from day one for the Panthers this coming season. He has 30-plus receptions each of his first two seasons in the NFL. Coker has really good hands, failing to drop a pass each of his first two years. He is an improving route runner that can make plays after the catch. Coker is a big receiver that can get down the field in a hurry.
57.outlook: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker was an early offseason sleeper candidate after his budding chemistry with Bryce Young was put on display down the stretch of the 2025 season and in the Panthers' Wild Card loss to the Rams, in which he recorded a career-high 134 receiving yards and a touchdown. Coker began the season on injured reserve as the result of a strained quad, and he started slowly after missing six games. Over his final six games of the season, however, including the playoffs, Coker averaged 63 receiving yards per contest and scored four touchdowns, tied for the seventh-most by any receiver in that stretch. The Panthers have since added John Metchie III in free agency and spent a third-round pick on Chris Brazzell II in the NFL Draft. While neither projects as an insurmountable barrier to targets, they've added enough uncertainty to the receiver room to push Coker down to RotoBaller's WR49, making him even more of a bargain in the late rounds of drafts. Managers who were in on Coker when everybody could see the path should be even more in at his current cost. He projects to be the primary slot receiver in an offense whose weak tight end room led to the seventh-highest rate of 11 personnel in the league in 2025, and at 6'3" and 213 pounds, he's got the size to kick outside in two-receiver sets alongside 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year Tetairoa McMillan. Coker has been an easy player to root for since the Panthers picked him up as an undrafted free agent out of Holy Cross in 2024, and 2026 is lining up cleanly for a potential breakout season.

58.name: Omar Cooper Jr.
58.comment: The Jets selected Cooper with the 30th overall pick in this year's draft. He has a great chance to start right away in this offense, playing opposite Garrett Wilson. Cooper is a good compliment to Wilson. He is a big, strong receiver that can make plays after contact. He catches the ball well and can make plays at all three levels. His route running could use a little work and he isn't always great on the contested catch despite his size.
58.outlook: New York Jets wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. broke out in his fourth season with Indiana, collecting 69 receptions for 937 yards and 13 touchdowns. He was a key piece on the Hoosiers' run to the College Football Playoff National Championship and served as Fernando Mendoza's WR1. His 2025 performance shot him up draft boards, and he landed with the New York Jets with the No. 30 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. His first-round draft capital makes him a valuable rookie draft pick in an underwhelming class, but his chances of breaking out as a rookie are low. For one, Cooper will be catching passes from Geno Smith, who was among the worst quarterbacks in the league last season. Secondly, he'll be competing with Garrett Wilson and fellow rookie Kenyon Sadiq for targets. Lastly, he's a flawed prospect to begin with, given his late breakout age (21.7). The Jets' offense has been undesirable for fantasy football for several years, and that's not set up to change in 2026. Cooper is an interesting dart throw in deep setups, but he could be unrosterable for the majority of his debut campaign. Wilson should be expected to remain the clear alpha wide receiver in New York.

59.name: Khalil Shakir
59.comment: Shakir was the most consistent receiver for the Bills once again, getting 70-plus receptions for the second straight season. He had 72 receptions for 719 and four touchdowns, finishing 35th overall in fantasy receiver scoring. Shakir had double-digit fantasy points nine of 16 games. Shakir should continue to be a big part of the Bills offense this year, getting plenty of targets as the top possession receiver for the team. Shakir has top speed and elite hands (six drops in four seasons). He has very good moves in space and can make plays after the catch. He lacks some strength but that hasn't held him back much to date.
59.outlook: Buffalo Bills wide receiver Khalil Shakir led the receiving room with 72 catches for 719 yards on 95 targets, but could only parlay that into four touchdowns and three top-25 PPR weekly finishes. There was very little competition for looks from Josh Allen, who remains the clear focal point of the offense. And now, DJ Moore should offer a viable No. 1 WR on the perimeter, which can free up Shakir from the slot, but also eliminates any expectation of rising volume. We'd expect a fourth straight season with a catch rate north of 75% in a top offense, though the healthy 23.5% first-read rate could dip. His role may remain unchanged, with Moore's production coming from Keon Coleman, Joshua Palmer, and the rest. Even so, Dalton Kincaid may also finally enjoy good health and siphon looks across 17 games. Shakir's half-PPR ADP around pick 132 puts him in that Round 11/12 spot for 12-teamers, where nabbing a safe yet boring WR4 works for many who took big swings early.

60.name: Malachi Fields
60.comment: Fields was a third-round pick for the Giants in this year's draft. Fields is likely to be the No. 2 or 3 receiver for the Giants his rookie season. He is a tall, strong receiver. Fields is a good route runner that uses his frame well to shield off defenders and catch passes. He does lack a little speed, making him just alright on the deep route.
60.outlook: Fields is intriguing, possibly starting in an emerging Giants offense. He could end up with some of the better numbers for this rookie receiving class. He is worth a shot as a No. 4 or 5 fantasy receiver, getting around 60 receptions for 700 yards and five touchdowns.

61.name: Jalen Tolbert
61.comment: Tolbert moved to more of a reserve role last year, getting a lot less work than the previous year with the Cowboys. He had 18 receptions for 203 yards, his lowest totals since his rookie season. Tolbert signed with the Dolphins and should get a chance to compete for a starting job with his new team. Miami has plenty of openings at receiver. Tolbert is a great athlete that can do a little bit of everything at receiver. He will drop some passes, though, and lacks a little consistency. And he makes few plays after contact because of a lack of size.
61.outlook: Tolbert is a good late-round gamble. He could emerge as a top playmaker in this offense. Tolbert could get around 60 receptions for 800 yards and five touchdowns.

62.name: Matthew Golden
62.comment: Golden had a disappointing rookie season. He struggled to find consistency, ending year one with just 29 receptions for 361 yards while failing to find the end zone. He came off the bench most weeks and his big games were few and far between. Golden had double-digit fantasy points just three games and didn't reach that mark after Week 6. Golden has a chance to play a bigger role this season but will need a strong offseason and camp for that to happen. He has a lot to prove after last year. Golden has game-changing speed and does his best work on the deep ball. He also does really well after the catch, having great moves in space. Golden also does well on the contested catch and can make the tough catch when needed. He needs some work on his entire route tree, though, and consistency was a huge issue last year.
62.outlook: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Matthew Golden disappointed as a rookie: 29 catches for 361 yards and zero touchdowns in 14 games, despite being the team's first first-round wide receiver selection since 2002. Team brass isn't giving up on Golden just yet, however. The former Texas Longhorn has further entrenched himself among the main receiver rotation with the departures of target leader Romeo Doubs (New England) and Dontayvion Wicks (Philadelphia). That leaves Golden, Christian Watson, and Jayden Reed, who almost exclusively lines up in the slot, as the starting trio. While his talent remains a question, this is a golden (no pun intended) opportunity for the sophomore to make his impact. His speed (4.29 40-yard dash at the NFL Combine in 2025) makes him an enticing selection in fantasy drafts this summer. Golden is a high-upside WR5 in RotoBaller's wide receiver rankings.

63.name: Denzel Boston
63.comment: Boston was selected by the Browns in the second round of this year's draft. He should compete immediately for a starting role in the Browns offense. He is a big, strong receiver that uses his size and strength to his advantage. He does really well on the contested catch. He lacks al little elite speed for the position, which can hold him back a little when trying to stretch the field. Boston has a lot to compete with for playing time in Cleveland but should be given every opportunity to play a big role as a rookie.
63.outlook: For many, seeing wide receiver Denzel Boston slide to the Cleveland Browns in the second round came as a surprise. Even more surprising was the fact that the Browns double-dipped at the wide receiver position, having selected KC Concepcion 15 picks before the Boston selection. The additions of Boston and Concepcion are aimed at bolstering a passing attack that mustered just 165.2 passing yards per game (second-fewest) in 2025. With Jerry Jeudy and Concepcion as the likely receivers playing alongside Boston, the former Washington Husky offers something the other two don't, and that's size. Jeudy measures in at 6'1 and 195 pounds, while Concepcion is a generous 5'11, 190 pounds. Neither of which comes across as a true threat should the Browns reach the endzone. As for Boston, his 6'4, 210-pound physique, along with his elite catching radius and 62% career contested-catch rate, makes him an ideal target inside the 20. With no real competition in Cleveland for Boston at the X receiver spot, the 22-year-old is set to lead the Browns' pass catchers in fantasy production thanks to a higher projected touchdown rate. Boston has an ADP of 166 on Sleeper in redraft leagues, making him a value as RotoBaller currently ranks the rookie wideout 148th overall heading into upcoming fantasy football drafts.

64.name: Quentin Johnston
64.comment: Johnston has two straight very similar seasons, getting a chance to start most of the year with the Chargers. He was up and down but his numbers in the end weren't too bad, finishing with 51 receptions for 735 yards and eight touchdowns. He was 33rd overall in fantasy receiver scoring. Johnston was erratic for fantasy teams, having double-digit fantasy points nine games but went two games without even a reception. He has a lot to compete with for targets in Los Angeles but should get his weekly chances once again. Johnston has a big-time skillset for the position. He has a great blend of speed and size. He can get downfield in a hurry. He also is a huge target because of his size and wingspan. Johnston remains an iffy route runner and will drop some passes (12 for his career).
64.outlook: Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Quentin Johnston is entering his fourth year in the NFL, coming off of his best statistical season in which he recorded 51 catches for 735 yards and eight touchdowns. Johnston was widely regarded as a bust after a shaky rookie season, but the former first-rounder has emerged as a steady contributor in the offense. Johnston led the Chargers in receiving touchdowns in 2025, and finished just 54 yards behind leading receiver Ladd McConkey. His play was inconsistent, with a big statistical spike at the beginning of the season and again in Weeks 16-17. If Keenan Allen, who is currently a free agent, does not return, Johnston could see more consistent usage in 2026.

65.name: Tank Dell
65.comment: Dell didn't play at all last season after suffering a gruesome injury the season before. He dislocated his kneecap and suffered a torn ACL, MCL and LCL. Dell has huge question marks going forward, wondering if he can return to past form. But if he comes back healthy and his usual self, Dell can play a big role in this offense. Dell has 10 touchdowns in 25 games and averages 14.0 yards per reception for his career. Dell is a big-play threat. He has game-changing speed and can get to the next level in a hurry. He has a knack for finding the end zone. Dell lacks some size, though, and will struggle with the contested catch. He has 10 drops in two seasons.
65.outlook: Dell is a big risk as he recovers from his major injuries. And once he returns, you have to have to wonder if he will be the same player. That remains to be seen. Dell might be worth the risk as a deep reserve, hoping he regains some past magic.

66.name: Zachariah Branch
66.comment: Atlanta selected Branch in the third round of this year's draft. He is a very small receiver but a great fit out of the slot. He excelled in that area in college. He has great burst and quickness. Branch makes a lot of plays after the catch and is dangerous in the open field. He rarely caught anything down the field in college, though, and his route running can be a little sloppy. The Falcons have all sorts of openings at receiver, so Branch has a chance to be the slot receiver from day one his rookie season.
66.outlook: The Atlanta Falcons selected former USC and Georgia speedster Zachariah Branch in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Atlanta's offense has been very heavily dependent on Bijan Robinson, Drake London, and Kyle Pitts Sr. for the past few seasons. Beyond those three weapons, there hasn't been another consistent producer. In order for Branch to see the field in two receiver sets, he just needs to beat out Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus. He may be smaller, standing 5-foot-9, but Branch's speed brings an element to the Falcons' offense that wasn't there before. Expect him to see schemed touches from day one.

67.name: Malik Washington
67.comment: Washington served as the No. 3 receiver for the Dolphins most weeks of his second season. He had 46 receptions for 317 yards and three touchdowns, finishing 53rd overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He did not have more than 50-receiving yards in a single game. Washington did have multiple receptions all but four games. The Dolphins had all sorts of departures at receiver this offseason, so Washington could play a big role if he earns the trust of the coaching staff and new starting quarterback, Malik Willis. Washington is a good fit for the slot. He is a small receiver that runs good routes and does well after the catch. Washington excels at turning a short pass into a big play. He also catches the ball very well. Washington does lack a little speed for the position and won't do much down the field.
67.outlook: Washington has a chance to take another stop forward this year but probably isn't going to be a huge fantasy factor. He might be worth some spot starts but that is about it. His ceiling is a little limited. Washington can get around 60 receptions for 600 yards and a few scores.

68.name: Stefon Diggs
68.comment: Diggs was the top receiver for the Patriots last year, finishing 16th overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He had a great season in the Patriots suddenly high-powered offense. Diggs had the seventh 1,000-yard season of his career. He was very consistent, having double-digit fantasy points 10 of 17 games. There were a few concerns for Diggs, though. He is 32 years old and had the lowest ADOT of his career (8.5). He can still serve a starting role well but might be more of a possession receiver at this stage of his career. Diggs is a pretty physical receiver that does well in making plays all over the field. He isn't afraid to go over the middle and make the tough catch. He also has good moves in space and top hands.
68.outlook: Diggs seems a long shot to replicate last year. A regression in numbers would not be a surprise. Consider him a No. 3 or 4 fantasy receiver. Look for around 60 receptions, 700 yards and three or four touchdowns.

69.name: Devaughn Vele
69.comment: Vele was traded to the Saints last year and got some work with his new team. He started to really posted some good numbers after Week 10 but a shoulder injury late in the year cut his season short. It was bad timing for Vele. He had 19 receptions for 239 yards and a touchdown his last four games played. Vele has a chance to earn a big role with the Saints this year, possibly starting or serving as the No. 3. Vele has 66 receptions in two seasons. Vele is a good route runner for a young player and catches the ball well. He does lack some speed and won't do a ton after the catch.
69.outlook: Vele is a good late-round gamble. He might be able to build on his strong finish to last year. He could get 60 receptions for 700 yards and a few scores.

70.name: Adonai Mitchell
70.comment: Mitchell started his second season with the Colts last year but was dealt about halfway through the season, which was good news for him. He got a lot more playing time with the Jets, catching 24 passes for 301 yards and two touchdowns. He had just nine receptions in eight games for the Colts before heading to the Jets. Mitchell started four games for New York and should complete for a starting job this coming year. Mitchell has 20-plus receptions each of his first two seasons in the NFL. Mitchell has top speed and can run by defenders in a hurry. His size also gives him an advantage over defenders when it comes to jump balls and contested catches. Mitchell remains a bit of a raw product, though, and still has work to do as a route runner.
70.outlook: Mitchell is going to have some big games but likely disappear in others. He might not be as consistent as fantasy owners hope. Mitchell is worth a late-round look for fantasy owners because of his big-game potential. He can get 50 receptions for 700 yards and a few touchdowns.

71.name: Ja'Kobi Lane
71.comment: Lane was a third-round selection by the Ravens in this year's draft. He seems a great compliment to Zay Flowers at receiver. Lane is a big receiver that can stretch the field and make the acrobatic catch. He gets in and out of his breaks well for a man of his size. He lacks a little strength for the position and might need to bulk up to be a more complete receiver in the pro game. With a strong camp and preseason, Lane could challenge for a starting job his rookie season.
71.outlook: Lane is an intriguing fantasy player. He could emerge in a hurry in this offense, giving him late-round value come draft day. Look for him to get around 50 receptions for 700 yards and a few scores.

72.name: Jayden Higgins
72.comment: Higgins had a so-so rookie season, getting a chance to start 10 of 17 games. He had 41 receptions for 525 yards and six touchdowns. Higgins was 46th overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He had more than 80 yards just one game all year but did reach double-digit fantasy points five of his last nine games. Higgins was a little more consistent down the stretch. He will look to earn a starting job from day one this year but has some competition for that job. Higgins is a big receiver that runs very good routes and has plus hands. He does well in shielding the defender and making the contested catch. His size also allows him to beat press coverage, which is a plus for a young player. He isn't great after the catch, though, and he failed to make many big plays down the field last season.
72.outlook: Houston Texans wide receiver Jayden Higgins, a second-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, appeared in all 17 games as a rookie and recorded 41 receptions for 525 yards and six touchdowns. While he got off to a somewhat slow start, Higgins emerged as a top-30 fantasy receiver during the middle portion of the season, averaging more than eight fantasy points per game and scoring three touchdowns from Weeks 8 through 14. Higgins should see additional opportunities in 2026 following the departure of veteran receiver Christian Kirk. Of course, the Texans also selected Higgins' Iowa State teammate, Jaylin Noel, in the third round of last year's draft. However, Noel's rookie-year usage suggests he will primarily operate out of the slot, while Higgins and Nico Collins handle the majority of the snaps on the outside and in two-receiver sets. Fantasy managers considering Higgins will likely base their evaluation on quarterback C.J. Stroud. Although Stroud has struggled at times over the past two seasons, he showcased elite upside as a rookie and should benefit from entering his second year in offensive coordinator Nick Caley's system. If the Texans' offense takes a step forward, Higgins could emerge as one of the best values in fantasy football, considering he is currently being drafted as a WR5 in the 12th round.

73.name: Jahan Dotson
73.comment: Dotson was the No. 3 receiver for the Eagles much of last season but didn't do a whole lot in that role, finishing with very similar numbers to his first season with the team. He had 18 receptions for 262 yards and a touchdown. He has not topped 20 receptions two straight season. Dotson had just a game with double-digit fantasy points. He signed with the Falcons this offseason and hopes to earn a starting job with opposite Drake London. Dotson has some starting experience but hasn't exactly excelled in that role. Dotson is an explosive player that does well at all levels. He can turn a short pass into a big play or just run past defenders to make a big play down the field. He lacks some consistency, though, and hasn't exactly lived up to expectations to date.
73.outlook: Dotson has a chance to set career highs if he earns a starting job but don't expect a monster season. He'll be hit or miss in an offense that hasn't exactly supported the other starter for fantasy purposes. Dotson can get around 50 receptions for 650 yards and a few scores.

74.name: Tre Tucker
74.comment: Tucker was the most consistent receiver for the Raiders last year but that isn't saying much. He had career highs across the board in receptions (57), yards (696) and touchdowns (five). Tucker finished 37th overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He didn't have many big fantasy games outside a monster performance in Week 3 (eight receptions for 145 yards and three touchdowns). Tucker had just four other games all year with double-digit fantasy points despite starting all 17 games. Tucker will have more competition for work this year but seems likely to at least keep the No. 3 job, a role he serves pretty well. Tucker has 45-plus receptions two straight seasons. Tucker is a small receiver that does well out of the slot. He can turn a short pass into a big play. His small size gets him pushed around in coverage and he can struggle with contested catches.
74.outlook: Tucker might have a hard time improving on last year. The one positive for him is a new quarterback throwing him passes. But even with that said, he could see a few less targets, getting around 50 receptions for 600 yards and a few scores. This makes him reserve material for fantasy teams.

75.name: Tyreek Hill
75.comment: Hill played four games before suffering a horrific knee injury. He dislocated his knee cap and tore multiple knee ligaments. Hill had 12-plus fantasy points three of four games before the injury. He was posting his usual solid numbers before the injury. Hill has a long road back from this terrible injury and might not even be ready for the start of the year. But once health, he will likely slide into a starting role once again. Hill has 1,200-plus yards four of six seasons. Hill is a speed burner that can make all sorts of plays in the open field. He is small and lacks strength, but that hasn't slowed him down one bit since entering the league. Hill catches the ball well and is an improved route runner since early in his career. He also can make big plays in the running game, having 95-plus rushing yards four times.
75.outlook: Hill is a real wild card. He is returning from a terrible injury and is 32 years old. The chances of him producing the big numbers from earlier in his career seem slim. Take him as a No. 3 or 4 receiver and hope for some big games along the way. He can get around 60 receptions for 800 yards and four or five touchdowns.

76.name: Travis Hunter
76.comment: Hunter played more receiver than cornerback his rookie season but had his year cut short because of a knee injury. He was just starting to find his footing before getting hurt, hitting the 100-yard mark his last game played. Hunter had 28 receptions for 298 yards and a touchdown in seven games. Hunter will continue to play both sides of the ball and could send up playing more defense than offense in year two. Jacksonville already has three solid options ahead of him on the depth chart. Hunter will get some touches on a weekly basis as a receiver but probably not a ton. Hunter is a dynamic player after the catch. He also is really good at getting open, using his speed and athleticism. He also is a great straight-line runner that can run by defenders in a hurry.
76.outlook: The Jacksonville Jaguars made an aggressive move in 2025, giving up multiple first-round picks to be in position to select Travis Hunter (knee), who won the Heisman Trophy at wide receiver and cornerback with Colorado in 2024, with last year's No. 2 overall pick. At that time, Hunter's ability to contribute in fantasy football was a bit of a question mark because of his defensive responsibilities, and optimistic managers were not rewarded. Hunter ended up catching just 28 passes (on 45 targets) for 298 yards and just one touchdown over seven games. After his best effort in London against the Rams (101 yards and a score) in Week 7, he injured his right knee in practice - an injury that ultimately cost him the rest of his rookie campaign. The 23-year-old should be a "full go" for training camp. Jacksonville acquired Jakobi Meyers from the Raiders to aid Brian Thomas Jr. for the playoff-bound squad, and Parker Washington broke out with 26 catches for 454 yards and three touchdowns over the team's final four contests (including playoffs). That leaves Hunter as a non-essential member of Jacksonville's receiving group. This doesn't help his case for a larger role on offense, as his health and adaptation to the pro level are both top priorities for the team. In limited spurts, the former collegiate superstar showed off the talent that made him a top-five pick. He's an intriguing buy in dynasty formats at a cost that is tanking due to offseason rumors that he'll be primarily a cornerback in 2026 after the team let DB Greg Newsome walk in free agency. However, in redraft formats, Hunter's 193rd-overall slot in RotoBaller's PPR rankings suggests he's a bit of an afterthought. A handful of designed touches to showcase his talent might still be on the menu. Still, Hunter would need to be a cluster injury away from Jacksonville's wide receiving corps this season to be a featured member of their passing attack.

77.name: Darnell Mooney
77.comment: Mooney took a step backwards in year two for the Falcons, getting a lot fewer chances. He started 15 games but had just 32 receptions for 443 yards and a touchdown. He was just eight yards shy of a 1,000-yard season the previous year. Mooney did not have a single game with double-digit fantasy points and had more than 50 yards just twice. He gets a fresh start this year with the Giants and will be given a chance to win a starting job opposite Malik Nabers. Mooney has one 1,000-yard season for his career and fewer than 500 yards three of four seasons. Mooney is a small receiver but has great moves in space and top speed. He will make the tough catch in traffic and plenty of plays after the catch. He will drop some passes, though, and struggle with consistency at times.
77.outlook: Mooney might be worth a late-round gamble. There is a chance for him to rebound if he can win a starting job in this emerging offense. For now, look for around 50 receptions for 650 yard and three or so touchdowns.

78.name: Antonio Williams
78.comment: The Commanders picked Williams in the third round of this year's draft. He is expected to serve as the No. 3 receiver for the team his rookie season. Williams does his best work out of the slot. He does well getting in and out of his breaks in a hurry. Williams has good quickness and a knack for getting open. He will drop some passes and is not much of a deep threat.
78.outlook: The Washington Commanders selected wideout Antonio Williams in the third round of April's draft. The former Clemson product immediately projects as their No. 2 receiver behind Terry McLaurin. The lack of premier pass-catching options in the Commanders' passing game increases Williams' volume outlook. He was a four-year contributor at Clemson and exited the program with the fourth most career receptions (208) and tied for the fourth most touchdown receptions (21) in school history. Williams broke out as a junior, hauling in 75 catches for 904 yards and 11 touchdowns, which led the ACC. His production dipped last season while battling injuries, but he displayed great ball skills by improving his drop rate from 9.6 percent to 1.8 percent. Williams is seen as a smooth operator as a route runner and is praised for his ability to create separation at all three levels of the field. Williams has an opportunity to be a featured target in the Washington passing offense from the slot and "Z" receiver position in David Blough's offense. Blough is anticipated to run a version of Ben Johnson's offense, which centered around Amon-Ra St. Brown as the slot receiver in Detroit. Additionally, Jayden Daniels will be looking for a security blanket over the middle of the field on quick routes with the departure of Zach Ertz. Ertz has caught the most passes (81) and the second-most touchdowns in the red zone (eight) from Daniels. Williams may struggle to surpass 1,000 receiving yards, but his outstanding separation skills and large catch radius will catch the eye of Daniels more often than not.

79.name: Tre Harris
79.comment: Harris had a tough time getting consistent work his rookie season. He played every game but had just 30 receptions for 324 yards and a touchdown. He did not reach double-digit fantasy points in a single game. Harris might be stuck in a similar reserve role this season for the Chargers. Harris is a good combination of size and speed. He can get down the field in a hurry. His route running needs a little work, being a little one-dimensional at this stage of his career.
79.outlook: There probably won't be a rookie who gets more of a "pass" for a poor 2025 campaign than Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Tre' Harris. After the team signed Keenan Allen in training camp, Allen, Ladd McConkey, and former first-round pick Quentin Johnston were entrenched as the team's top-three wide receivers. Harris played north of 65% of the snaps in just three games, and he managed just 30 catches (on 43 targets) for the season. Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh was complimentary of Harris' blocking and versatility after a Week 6 win in Miami, but Harris saw just 32 total targets after that contest. To this point, Allen remains unsigned, which clears the way for the former Ole Miss star in three-receiver sets, and Johnston's historical inconsistency could open the door to a legitimate target share. Harris was best known as a prospect for a hyper-productive 2024 campaign, during which he set the FBS record for yards per route run (5.12) among players who ran at least 200 routes in a season, according to Pro Football Focus. So, it was surprising to see him rarely pop at just 10.8 yards per reception and one total touchdown. The Chargers' internal chaos, including offensive line injuries and then OC Greg Roman calling plays, didn't help. Now, he'll look to carve out a role in new playcaller Mike McDaniel's offense, which produced massive seasons for Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle in Miami. McConkey and Johnston aren't the only competition; L.A.'s tight end duo, Oronde Gadsden II and recently signed David Njoku, will also demand their share of looks. Perhaps due to the team's immense depth at pass catcher, RotoBaller's PPR rankings (219th overall) leave Harris with an undraftable outlook, but you also can't rule him out entirely from the chance to lead the Bolts in total targets. Receivers with rookie years as quiet as Harris' don't typically pan out. Still, the talent, draft capital, and circumstances at play could result in the 6-foot-3" wideout becoming an all-time exception.

80.name: Germie Bernard
80.comment: The Steelers picked Bernard in the second round of this year's draft. He should slot into the No. 3 receiver role for the team his rookie year, playing alongside DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman. Bernard is a very good route runner for a young player. He has good size for the position and catches the ball well. Bernard does a great job of just getting open. He lacks a little bit of a second gear, making him a likely so-so deep threat at the NFL level.
80.outlook: The Pittsburgh Steelers selected wideout Germie Bernard with the 47th overall pick in April's draft. The former Alabama standout currently projects as the Steelers' No. 3 pass catcher and starting slot receiver. Bernard was a Swiss Army Knife for three of his four years in college, finding ways to contribute despite playing in talented receiver rooms. The blue-collar wideout was Alabama's leading receiver in his final two seasons and served as a chess piece in the run and pass game. Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy has heavily used 11-personnel as a play-caller, which provides Bernard with an immediate opportunity to play. Aaron Rodgers undercenter also favors Bernard's fantasy outlook this season. In 2025, Rodgers had the fewest completed air yards (1,203) and the second most pass yards after the catch (2,119) of quarterbacks who started at least 15 games. Additionally, Rodgers had one of the lowest average depths of target (6.4) and one of the fastest average times to throw (2.56 seconds) in the league according to PFF. These stats blend well with Bernard, who was an elite route runner on short, quick routes with great vision and contact balance after the catch. At this stage in Rodgers' career, Bernard might become Rodgers' favorite target and push to lead the Steelers in targets this season.

81.name: Jalen McMillan
81.comment: A neck injury and the emergence of rookie Emeka Egbuka really put a damper on McMillan's season last year. He played just four games, getting 12 catches for 178 yards. McMillan had a promising rookie season, fishing with 37 receptions, but was unable to build on that. The departure of Mike Evans should be a positive for McMillan this year, giving him the clear No. 3 receiver job for him. McMillan can serve the slot role very well. McMillan is a good route runner for a young player. He knows how to get open out of the slot. He can struggle some with the contested catch and press coverage.
81.outlook: Tampa Bay Buccaneers wide receiver Jalen McMillan lost nearly all of the 2025 season after a scary neck/spine injury during the preseason, which held him out until Week 15. That was the same week that Mike Evans returned to play, which forced McMillan into a WR3/4 rotation with Emeka Egbuka behind Chris Godwin Jr. and Evans. The only game that McMillan saw more than three targets was a nine-look Week 17 that produced a 7-114-0 receiving line. Much of the post-Evans hype in Tampa has shifted to Egbuka, though McMillan cannot be overlooked. He'll vie for WR3 work with Tez Johnson and rookie Ted Hurst, but he has a size advantage over Johnson and the experience edge over Hurst. Murmurs around new offensive coordinator Zac Robinson's 12 personnel rate in Atlanta can be quieted by the fact that the Falcons' WR depth was nowhere near the 2026 Bucs. At his June half-PPR ADP of 155 as the WR58, McMillan provides a fun upside gamble with an above-average QB and a defense that can yield shootout scripts.

82.name: Christian Kirk
82.comment: Kirk fell down the depth chart in Houston last year and had a disappointing season. He caught 28 passes for 239 yards and a touchdown in 13 games. He had two games with double-digit fantasy points. Kirk played his best football in the Texans two playoff games, finishing with 10 receptions for 164 yards and two touchdowns on 15 targets. Kirk has fewer than 400 yards two straight seasons. He signed with the 49ers and should become the No. 3 receiver for his new team. A move to the 49ers offense could be a positive for Kirk, playing in a scheme that might fit him a little better. Kirk has one 1,000-yard season for his career but topped 75 receptions two of eight years. Kirk doesn't have great size, but is good on underneath routes and catches the ball well. He doesn't make a lot of big plays in the passing game but is capable because of his top speed. Kirk does his best work on shorter routes, making him a good move the chains player.
82.outlook: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Christian Kirk was limited to 13 games with the Texans due to hamstring issues in 2025. It was the third consecutive season that Kirk missed multiple weeks due to injury, though he was spared the trips to injured reserve that upended his 2023 and 2024 campaigns. Kirk finished the year with 28 receptions for 239 yards and one touchdown on 52 targets, the least productive season in his eight-year career. After signing with San Francisco in March, Kirk will try for better results in Kyle Shanahan's offense. It might be difficult for Kirk to get quarterback Brock Purdy's attention in a receiver group where upstart Ricky Pearsall and fellow free agent Mike Evans figure to top the depth chart, and George Kittle (Achilles) and Christian McCaffrey will demand a hefty target share of their own. Kirk is listed as the WR87 in RotoBaller's current rankings. He will likely be a better role player on the field than a fantasy asset and can be ignored in drafts.

83.name: Deebo Samuel
83.comment: Samuel had a solid first season in Washington, finishing 24th overall in fantasy receiver scoring. He had eight games with double-digit fantasy points, including four games with 20-plus points. Samuel was a little inconsistent, having 10 games with fewer than 50-receiving yards. He had some top-heavy numbers but injuries at quarterback didn't help matters for Samuel. He should continue to be a big part of the Commanders offense going forward. Samuel has one 1,000-yard receiving season for his career. Injuries are always a concern for him, missing time each of his first seven seasons in the league. Samuel is a good route runner that can make plenty of plays after the catch. He also can be used all over the field as a running back, in the slot or on the outside. He is a tough cover for the opposition because of his size and speed.
83.outlook: Samuel has been a top-10 fantasy receiver two seasons, so the potential for big things is there. Consider him more of a top-40 option at this stage of his career, though. He could be hit or miss once again. Samuel should be able to get around 60 receptions, 800 total yards and five scores.

84.name: Ricky Pearsall
84.comment: Pearsall had 100-yard games two of his first three to start last season but injury issued marred much of the rest of his season. He played just nine games overall, finishing with 36 receptions for 528 yards. He has struggled with injury each of his first two seasons. The 49ers lost some receivers this offseason, giving Pearsall a chance to rack up the targets this season. Pearsall is a good route runner that can make the tough catch in traffic. He can get pushed around in coverage a little, making him a better fit for the slot than the outside. Pearsall has very good hands, having one drop in two seasons. Injuries are a concern, playing 20 games in two seasons.
84.outlook: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Ricky Pearsall has had an unimaginable start to his NFL career, marked by injuries and flashes of fantasy-football stardom. After ending his rookie season on a tear, Pearsall was on track to fully break out in his sophomore season before spraining his PCL, which sidelined him for 8 games. In Weeks 1-4, Pearsall was first in yards per reception (16.4), second in average depth of target (15.9), third in deep-target rate (32.1%), and fourth in receiving yards (327), according to PFF data. In Year 3, Pearsall finds himself in an improved offense with the addition of Mike Evans and rookie wideout De'Zhaun Stribling. Evans will allow Pearsall to slide back into his natural slot and "Z" receiver role that he played at the end of his rookie season. Additionally, with Evans' Hall of Fame pedigree, defenses will gravitate toward him, allowing Pearsall to operate freely against lesser defensive backs. Emeka Egbuka was the beneficiary of this a year ago when he was the WR10 overall with Evans on the field before injuries. On paper, the 49ers' passing game looks crowded, which likely contributes to Pearsall being drafted outside of the Top-35 receivers. However, Stribling projects as a developmental rookie, George Kittle is rehabbing from a torn Achilles, and Christian McCaffrey is a major regression candidate after his 2025 season. Pearsall has a chance to secure a healthy amount of targets in a high-powered offense. These factors make Pearsall a receiver to prioritize in the middle-to-late rounds of fantasy drafts.

85.name: Tutu Atwell
85.comment: Atwell saw a big dip in playing time last year with the Rams, getting six receptors for 192 yards and a touchdown in 10 games. The positive was he made some really big plays, averaging a robust 32 yards per reception. He had 35-plus receptions two straight seasons before last year. He signed with the Dolphins this offseason and has a good chance to play a big role with his new team, a team that has plenty of openings at receiver. Atwell is a speed burner. He has great moves in space and is a tough cover out of the slot because of his quickness. He can get open in a hurry and make plays in space. He is really small, though, and can get pushed around in coverage.
85.outlook: Atwell should see a big uptick in playing time but likely is more depth material than anything for fantasy teams. He is going to get some weekly catches but his ceiling isn't super high in this offseason. Atwell can get around 40 receptions for 600 yards and a few scores.

86.name: Caleb Douglas
86.comment: The Dolphins took Douglas in the third round of this year's draft. He has a chance to get playing time right away in an offense lacking weapons in the passing game. Douglas is a tall receiver with a big catch radius. He also has good speed for the position. Douglas does well in making the acrobatic catch. He lacks a little physicality and lacked some consistency in college.
86.outlook: If you survey the front office from all 32 teams around the league, 31 of those times would tell you that the Miami Dolphins reached on the selection of Caleb Douglas. Miami was likely the only team that had a third-round grade on Douglas. With the turnover of the Dolphins roster, Douglas is in the conversation of potentially being fantasy relevant. Miami cut ties with both Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle, who have each been staples of the Dolphins' passing attack over the last few seasons, giving way to the likes of Jalen Tolbert, Tutu Atwell, Malik Washington, Jalen Reagor, and Kevin Coleman Jr. Miami's best receiver may not be able to suit up this season, as Chris Bell is recovering from an ACL injury. Miami's current top three receiver projection features a combined total of 70 receptions for 712 receiving yards, with Washington responsible for a majority of that, hauling in 46 passes for 317 yards last year. On my rosters, Douglas wouldn't even get a sniff. After a back-to-back 54-plus reception seasons resulting in at least 840 receiving yards, Douglas may be one of the best receivers in one of the worst receiver rooms in the NFL.

87.name: Brandon Aiyuk
87.comment: Aiyuik missed all of last season, recovering from a knee injury. There was all sorts of speculation that other stuff was going on besides the injury, so who knows what really happened last year? Aiyuk has played just seven games the last two years. He had two straight 1,000-yard seasons before that. Aiyuk gets a fresh start this year and will look to earn a big role with his new team, serving as the No. 1 receiver. Aiyuk has top speed and is explosive in the passing game, especially after the catch. He has grown a lot as a receiver since entering the league, showing much better consistency. Aiyuk has become one of the best all-around receivers in the game when healthy and playing.
87.outlook: Aiyuk has been a top-20 fantasy receiver two straight seasons before these last two seasons. He is a risk after last year, though. Who knows what is really going on with him? But if you want to take a chance, Aiyuk certainly has a high ceiling if all goes right for him. He can get 70 receptions for 1,000 yards and seven touchdowns.

88.name: Isaac TeSlaa
88.comment: TeSlaa was a top red-zone target his rookie year, scoring six touchdowns despite having just 16 receptions. He found the end zone four of his last six games to end the season. TeSlaa did not do much outside the scores, though, having more than 50 yards just a game. He could have a little bigger role this year offensively, getting more looks as the No. 3 receiver for the Lions. TeSlaa is good at going up and getting a ball from a defender, using his huge frame to his advantage. He is really good at finding the soft spot in coverages. TeSlaa could use some work on his route running to become a more complete receiver.
