88.outlook: Isaac TeSlaa demonstrated his ability to capitalize on his limited opportunities in 2025. Now, he is positioned to seize an expanded role during his second season. The Lions traded up 32 spots to seize TeSlaa in Round 3 (70th overall) of the 2025 NFL Draft. This transpired after TeSlaa accumulated 103 targets/62 receptions/896 receiving yards during the final two seasons of his collegiate career (2023-2024), while averaging 19.5 yards per reception in 2024. TeSlaa collected just 27 targets/16 receptions/239 receiving yards during 2025, but that did not impede him from securing 11 targets inside the red zone. He also accumulated six touchdowns and registered a 17.1% touchdown market share per Fantasy Points Data. 17 of TeSlaa's targets were captured from Weeks 13-17. That includes eight targets inside the red zone, which was second among Detroit's receiving weapons. TeSlaa also secured a 67.3% snap share and generated four touchdowns during that span. TeSlaa will encounter formidable competition for targets from Amon-Ra St. Brown. Jameson Williams, Sam LaPorta, and Jahmyr Gibbs. However, TeSlaa should operate as the Lions' WR3 following Kalif Raymond's departure during free agency. TeSlaa's increased role may not fuel consistent production in an offense that will be reconstructed under new coordinator Drew Petzing. However, the 6'4", 214-pound TeSlaa has the size and athleticism to create matchup issues for defenders and maintains the ability to function efficiently as a red-zone weapon. That makes him a viable target near his Round 18 ADP in best ball drafts (219/WR70), and his Round 20 ADP (230/WR83) in dynasty startups.

89.name: Brenen Thompson
89.comment: The Chargers took Thompson in the fourth round of this year's draft. Thompson is a really small receiver but has great speed and quickness. He does a good job of getting in and out of his breaks in a hurry. He is not a great deep threat despite his elite speed because of his lack of size and strength. Thompson has pretty good hands and displays good toughness. He will compete for a slot role in the Chargers offense as a rookie. New Chargers offense coordinator Mike McDaniel could find plenty of ways to use him offensively.
89.outlook: Thompson is an intriguing fantasy player. He has a chance to get weekly touches in this offense, making him worth a look as a fantasy receiver. He could get 600 total yards and a few scores.

90.name: Calvin Austin III
90.comment: Austin got some starts again last year but didn't do a whole lot with his chances. He had 31 receptions for 372 yards and three touchdowns in 14 games (seven starts). Austin had double-digit fantasy points four games. Austin has two straight seasons with 30-plus receptions. He signed with the Giants and will compete for their No. 3 job this coming season. Austin has some game-changing speed at the receiver spot. He lacks some size but has great speed and moves in space. He will make plays after the catch, turning a short pass into a big play. Austin can get pushed around because of his lack of size and will struggle with contested catches.
90.outlook: Austin could see a slight bump in production but is likely to be hit or miss once again. He will be a hard fantasy player to rust. He can get around 40 receptions for 500 yards and a few scores.

91.name: Keenan Allen
91.comment: A move back to the Chargers was a good one for Allen, catching 81 passes for 777 yards and four touchdowns. He was 28th overall in fantasy receiver scoring. His production did tail off as the season progressed, though. He had double-digit fantasy points three straight games to start his season and five of his first seven. He didn't hit that mark the rest of the year after Week 7. Allen is 34 years old, so age is a concern, especially if you consider his production hasn't been as good the last two seasons. He is more of a reserve receiver at this stage of his career. Allen has 1,100-plus yards five of nine seasons. He runs good routes and does a good job of just getting open. He is capable of turning a short play into a big one because of his quickness and moves in space.
91.outlook: Allen's age, injury issues in recent years and role in the offense are all big concerns. But even with that said, he produces when on the field and getting chances. He could be a top-50 receiver once again if all goes well for him. If he plays a full year, he can get 50 receptions for 500 yards and a few scores.

92.name: Keon Coleman
92.comment: There was hope that Coleman would elevate his game and take it to a new level in year two but that did not happen. He was erratic once again and disappeared more weeks than you would like. He had 38 receptions for 404 yards and four touchdowns. He had a huge Week 1, catching eight passes for 112 yards and a touchdown but did not have another game with more than 50 yards. Coleman is likely to be third or fourth on the depth chart this year after the addition of D.J. Moore to the Bills receiving room. Coleman has great size for the position and excels at making the acrobatic catch. He does a great job of winning contested catches and uses his size to his advantage. He lacks top-end speed for the position and can get pushed around in press coverage. Coleman also is just a so-so route runner.
92.outlook: Coleman will be a frustrating fantasy player once again. He'll post inconsistent numbers in his current role offensively. He is worth taking a shot on as a WR4 or WR5 because the upside is there, though. For now, look for around 40 receptions for 500 yards and three touchdowns.

93.name: Jack Bech
93.comment: Bech had a pretty quiet rookie season but showed some signs of life later in the season. He had 12 receptions from Week 13 to 16. He finished the year with 20 receptions for 224 yards. Bech reached double-digit fantasy points one game. The Raiders added some new talent at receiver this offseason but Bech can still play a big role with a strong camp and offseason. Bech is a pretty complete receiver. He runs good routes and has plus hands. He makes a lot of plays after the catch and looks more like a seasoned pro than a rookie. He does not have big-time speed and can get pushed around in coverage at times.
93.outlook: Bech can take a step forward in year two, especially with an upgrade at quarterback. But even with that said, he isn't quite a sure thing for fantasy teams. His ceiling isn't too high right now. He might be worth a late-round look for fantasy teams. Look for around 40 receptions for 500 yards and a few scores.

94.name: Chris Bell
94.comment: Bell was a third-round pick by the Dolphins in this year's draft. He is coming off a torn ACL and might not be ready for the start of the year. But once he is healthy, he could immediately compete for a starting job in this offense. Bell is a big, strong receiver that is good at moving the chains. He is tough to bring down with the ball in his hands. His route running needs improving and he is not much of a downfield threat.
94.outlook: The Miami Dolphins took wide receiver Chris Bell with the 94th pick in this April's NFL Draft, providing a much-needed addition to the team's receiving corps. Bell stands at 6-foot-2 and 222 pounds, giving him a strong frame to ward off defenders. The third-round rookie is coming off a productive season, as he finished 2025 with 72 receptions for 917 yards and six touchdowns on a 26.6-percent target share. Unfortunately, his campaign was cut short by a November ACL tear that has jeopardized his availability for Week 1. Because Miami will not be competitive, they have no reason to rush Bell back to action. When he returns, though, he may have ample opportunities working with new quarterback Malik Willis. The Dolphins have a lackluster set of receivers led by Malik Washington, Jalen Tolbert, and Tutu Atwell. They also drafted another receiver, Caleb Douglas, in the third round shortly before Bell. Bell has gone as the WR85 in drafts, reflecting his value as a late-round flyer. Rolling the dice on him is unlikely to bear fruit any time soon but could pay dividends down the line. Still, Bell is best left on waivers for the time being as he recovers.

95.name: Xavier Legette
95.comment: Legette actually got a little less work than his rookie season, finishing with 35 receptions for 363 yards and three touchdowns. He had three games with double-digit fantasy points, ending his season 69th overall in fantasy receiver scoring. Legette has failed to top 500-receiving yards each of his first two seasons in the NFL. He is likely to continue to rotate at receiver behind No. 1 option Tet McMillan. Legette is a big, strong receiver with plus speed. He does well with the contested catch and a good job of shielding off defenders with his size and strength. He can struggle some getting in and out of his breaks and drops can be an issue (nine for his career).
95.outlook: Legette has been little help to fantasy teams to date. He might do a little better than last season, but that isn't saying much. He probably isn't worth a roster spot outside of deeper formats. Look for around 40 catches for 400 yards and a few scores.

96.name: Pat Bryant
96.comment: Bryant got going later in his rookie year for the Broncos, emerging as the No. 3 receiver for the team. He had 31 receptions for 378 yards and a touchdown in 15 games. He had more than 50 yards just a game, though. He was 83rd overall in fantasy receiver scoring. Bryant was looking pretty good for a breakout season in year two until the Broncos traded for Jaylen Waddle. This likely pushes Bryant down to fourth on the depth chart. Bryant has good size for the position and can make some plays after the catch. He lacks a little explosion but his route running can help make up for that. Just don't expect a ton of big plays and drops can be an issue for him at times.
96.outlook: Bryant should get some targets but probably not enough to be a huge fantasy factor in his current role. He is likely fourth or fifth in the pecking order for receptions. He might get 40 receptions for 500 yards and a few touchdowns.

97.name: Elic Ayomanor
97.comment: Ayomanor was a bright spot at receiver for the Titans his rookie season. He ended up earning a starting role most of the season, finishing with 41 receptions for 515 yards and four touchdowns. Ayomanor had double-digit fantasy points three games. He failed to top 60 yards in any game. He is likely third or fourth on the depth chart this coming season in Tennessee. Ayomanor is a strong receiver that makes plays after contact. He can beat press coverage because of his strength. His route running could use some work and drops can be an issue for him (five last year).
97.outlook: Ayomanor is going to have a hard time getting consistent work behind at least two top options in the Titans passing game. He might be worth a late-round look, getting 40 catches for 500 yards and a few scores.

98.name: Chimere Dike
98.comment: Duke had a pretty productive rookie season, getting a chance to start 10 of 17 games. He got some playing more playing time than expected because of some injuries at receiver for the Titans. Dike had six games reaching double-digit fantasy points, finishing 48th overall in fantasy receiver scoring. Dike likely heads to more of a No. 3 receiver role for the Titans this coming season. Dike has great speed and is good after the catch. He will have some bad drops, though, and his route tree is a little limited right now. Dike should grow as a route runner with more seasoning.
98.outlook: Dike might have a hard time getting more consistent work this year, having at least two really good options ahead of him on the depth chart. He still might have some big games, making him worth a late-round look for fantasy teams. He can get around 40 receptions for 500 yards and a few scores.

99.name: Cooper Kupp
99.comment: Kupp played his first season with the Seahawks but didn't see a huge resurgence. Kupp had just 47 receptions for 593 yards and two touchdowns. Kupp was just 52nd overall in fantasy receiver scoring, hitting double-digit fantasy points just four games. He continued to show signs of decline. He could move to an even more reserve role this year for the Seahawks after the team re-signed Rashid Shaheed. Kupp has two 1,000-yard seasons for his career and topped 90 catches three times. He has played a full season just two times in eight years. Kupp has great hands and is a top route runner. He does lack some top-end speed, but he'll catch a ton of passes and doesn't let that slow him down one bit. He knows his limitations and makes the most of his abilities. He remains one of the better route runners in the game.
99.outlook: Seattle Seahawks receiver Cooper Kupp saw his production decline greatly in his first season with the team last year. Despite playing 16 games, Kupp had just 47 catches on 70 targets for 593 yards, all his worst figures since his eight-game 2018 campaign. Kupp also scored just twice, a new career low. He finished as the WR53, and he was the WR58 on a per-game basis with only 7.3 PPR points per game. Much of this was due to the dominance of teammate Jaxon Smith-Njigba, whose 35.9-percent target share topped all receivers. With the Seahawks returning Smith-Njigba in addition to Rashid Shaheed and Tory Horton, Kupp is facing competition for his starting gig. Moreover, this will be his age-33 season, and Kupp has already had major problems staying on the field, missing at least five games in each season from 2022 through 2024. While the Seattle offense should continue humming even without Kenneth Walker III, Kupp's fantasy value should continue dropping. He has been going as the WR82 in fantasy drafts, accurately reflecting that he is a late-round option at best. There should be more exciting choices on the board at that stage of your draft.

100.name: Andrei Iosivas
100.comment: Iosivas had a similar season to the previous one, finishing with 33 receptions for 435 yards and two touchdowns. He was the No. 3 for the Bengals most of the season and got some weekly chances in that role. He has 30-plus receptions and 400-plus yards each of the last two seasons. Iosivas is expected to play a similar role for the Bengals this year. He fits that role well. Iosivas runs good routes, has solid hands and does well on contested catches. Drops are a concern after having 12 in three seasons.
100.outlook: Iosivas has a little upside for the coming year. He could increase his catch total a little more once again but he has a lot to compete with for targets. He would look a lot better on another team. Look for around 40 receptions for 500 yards and a few touchdowns.
